nodes.name: Estimation of $\boldsymbol{r}$
nodes.statement: Throughout this paper, we assume that boldsymbolr = (r_1,r_2,r_3) is known, though in practice it needs to be estimated. Even in the matrix setting, rank estimation is known to be difficult, and there are many different procedures to estimate the rank for dimensionality reduction tailored to different statistical models (e.g., ). As our theory demonstrates, the matrix widehatG_k is approximately rank r_k, and, under our assumptions, will have r_k ``large'' eigenvalues and p_k - r_k ``small'' eigenvalues. Therefore, one principled approach to obtain a rank estimate is to look for an elbow in the scree plot of the hollowed Gram matrix widehatG_k from crefal:dd; see, for example, . However, in principle, any rank estimation procedure for matrices can be applied to widehatG_k. As this problem is worthwhile in its own right, we leave a more detailed explanation to future work.

Therefore, one principled approach to obtain a rank estimate is to look for an elbow in the scree plot of the hollowed Gram matrix $\mathbf{\widehat{G}}_k$ from \cref{al:dd}; see, for example, \cite{zhu_automatic_2006}.  However, in principle, any rank estimation procedure for matrices can be applied to $\mathbf{\widehat{G}}_k$.  As this problem is worthwhile in its own right, we leave a more detailed explanation to future work.

nodes.name: Comparison to Matrix Singular Vector Estimation
nodes.statement: Such a leading-order expansion has also been developed for symmetric matrix denoising in when both the row and column dimensions are of comparable size. One natural point of comparison is the corresponding error estimates for HOSVD (higher-order singular value decomposition), or similar procedures. In the tensor setting with p_k asymp p, each matricization is of order p times p^2, and the column dimension can be much larger than the row dimension. textcolorblackTherefore, when comparing asymptotic results for a p times p times p tensor to asymptotic results for a p_1 times p_2 matrix, the most natural point of comparison is to take p_1 asymp p and p_2 asymp p^2. In the subsequent discussion we will focus on matrices of dimension p_1 times p_2, but to translate the results to tensors, we will consider a generic p times p times p tensor, with p_1 asymp p and p_2 asymp p^2. In , who study entrywise singular vector analyses of rectangular matrices textcolorblackof dimension p_1 times p_2, it was shown that when lambda/sigma gtrsim sqrtp_max log(p_max) (which translates to the condition lambda/sigma gtrsim p sqrtlog(p))), that one has a leading-order expansion similar to the one presented in crefthm:eigenvectornormality_v1 (see their equation 3) for estimated singular vectors. However, the SNR condition in may be too stringent for tensors, particularly in the high-noise regime lambda/sigma asymp p^3/4 polylog(p). In , it was shown that when lambda/sigma asymp (p_1 p_2)^3/4 polylog(p) textcolorblack(which translates to the condition lambda/sigma gtrsim p^3/4 polylog(p)), that one has the leading-order expansion widehatU_k^S W_k - U_k &= Z_k V_k Lambda_k^-1 + Gamma( Z_k Z_k^top ) U_k Lambda_k^-2 + widetilde Psi^(k), where widetilde Psi^(k) is a residual term, widehatU_k^S are estimates of the left singular vectors of the underlying low-rank matrix obtained via the HeteroPCA algorithm, and Z_k and Lambda_k are the noise matrix and singular value matrix respectively. Observe that the term containing Gamma(Z_k Z_k^top) is quadratic in the noise Z_k--this additional quadratic term is dominant in the high-noise regime. Therefore, crefthm:eigenvectornormality_v1 demonstrates how HOOI uses the tensorial structure to effectively eliminate the additional (dominant) ``quadratic'' term in the regime p gtrsim lambda/sigma gtrsim p^3/4. These results textcolorblack(modulo logarithmic terms) are summarized in Table .

nodes.name: Adaptivity to Heteroskedasticity
nodes.statement: Note that the primary condition in crefthm:eigenvectornormality_v1 is essentially a signal-strength condition; in fact, this result continues to hold even if one does not have the condition sigma lesssim sigma_min in Assumption . It has been previously demonstrated in that in the absence of additional structure, heteroskedasticity may require additional debiasing for matrix singular vector estimation. In contrast, the leading-order expansion in crefthm:eigenvectornormality_v1 continues to hold even with heteroskedasticity (provided one initializes with diagonal deletion), which further demonstrates that tensor SVD is adaptive to unknown variance profiles. This phenomenon has also been discussed in a perturbative sense in .
nodes.raw_latex: Note that the primary condition in \cref{thm:eigenvectornormality_v1} is essentially a signal-strength condition;  in fact, this result continues to hold even if one does not have the condition $\sigma \lesssim \sigma_{\min}$ in Assumption \ref{ass:noise}.  It has been previously demonstrated in \cite{zhang_heteroskedastic_2022} that in the absence of additional structure, heteroskedasticity may require additional debiasing for matrix singular vector estimation.  In contrast, the leading-order expansion in \cref{thm:eigenvectornormality_v1} continues to hold \emph{even with heteroskedasticity} (provided one initializes with diagonal deletion), which further demonstrates that tensor SVD is \emph{adaptive} to unknown variance profiles.  This phenomenon has also been discussed in a perturbative sense in \cite{agterberg_estimating_2022}.

nodes.statement: The matrix Gamma^(m)_k is the same limiting covariance matrix as in Corollary 2 of (in the particular case the noise matrix therein has independent entries). However, a key feature is that crefthm:eigenvectornormality2_v1 holds when lambda/sigma asymp p^3/4 sqrtlog(p) (modulo factors of kappa, mu_0, and r), whereas the results of (when translated to the tensor setting) only hold when lambda/sigma asymp p sqrtlog(p), which shows how the additional tensor structure affects the limiting properties of the estimated singular vector components.

nodes.name: Comparison to Entrywise Distributional  Theory for Matrices
nodes.statement: crefthm:asymptoticnormalityentries_v1 can be compared to several results on entrywise distributional guarantees for low-rank matrices, such as Theorem 4.10 of or Theorem 6 of . Informally, the proof of crefthm:asymptoticnormalityentries_v1 shows that we have the approximate asymptotic expansion T_ijk - widehat T_ijk &approx e_i^top Z_1 V_1 V_1^top e_(j-1) p_3+k+e_j^top Z_2 V_2 V_2^top e_(k-1) p_1+i+e_k^top Z_3 V_3 V_3^top e_(i-1) p_2+j. Moreover, the asymptotic variance s^2_ijk is simply the variance of each of the three leading-order terms, ignoring cross-terms. While each of the three terms is not entirely uncorrelated (since they contain repetitions of elements of Z), we show that this correlation is negligible due to the incoherence of singular vectors. On the other hand, by slightly modifying the results in, for example, or , one can show that for a generic low-rank matrix M = U Lambda V^top of dimension p_1 times p_2, with p_1 asymp p_2, one has the approximate first-order decomposition M_ij - widehat M_ij &approx e_i^top Z V V^top e_j + e_j^top Z^top U U^top e_i, where widehat M is the truncated rank r SVD of the observed matrix M + Z, for Z consisting of independent noise. Hence, in contrast to the matrix case, the tensor case results in three (as opposed to two) leading-order perturbations, each of which is linear in the noise tensor Z, which shows how the tensorial structure manifests in the asymptotics.

nodes.name: Signal-Strength Requirement
nodes.statement: In addition to the signal-strength conditions from crefthm:eigenvectornormality_v1, crefthm:asymptoticnormalityentries_v1 also requires a lower bound on the magnitude of the appropriate rows of the matrices V_k. This condition implies a lower bound condition on the variance s^2_ijk of the form s_ijk gg maxbigg\ fracsigma r^3/2 sqrtlog(p)p^3/2, fracsigma^2 r^2 log(p)lambda sqrtp bigg\. Ignoring factors of r amounts to requiring that s_ijk gg maxbigg\ fracsigmasqrtlog(p)p^3/2, fracsigma^2 log(p)lambda sqrtp bigg\. A similar condition is required in the matrix setting in Theorem 4.10 of and Theorem 7 of . Informally, this condition is required so that there is enough signal within that corresponding entry of the underlying tensor. In the more challenging regime lambda/sigma asymp p^3/4polylog(p), this yields the condition s_ijk gg fracsigmap^5/4 polylog(p). Note that s_ijk is of order sigma times the size of the maximum of the corresponding rows of V_k. Since \| V_k \|_2,infty lesssim fracsqrtrp when mu_0 = O(1), we see that the corresponding rows are allowed to be as much as a factor of p^1/4 polylog(p) smaller than the maximum row norm, which covers a wide range of possible values. This regime is much broader than what is permitted in the matrix setting (e.g., Theorem 4.10 of ).

nodes.name: Signal-Strength Requirement
nodes.statement: We note that crefthm:civalidity_v1 requires an additional signal-strength condition to crefthm:asymptoticnormalityentries_v1. This additional requirement ensures that s^2_ijk gg fracsigma^3 log^3/2(p)lambda p^3/2, which implies that the variance dominates the bias in order to yield asymptotically valid confidence intervals. This is slightly more stringent than the condition in crefthm:asymptoticnormalityentries_v1. When lambda/sigma asymp p^3/4 polylog(p) and r = O(1), then this requirement essentially states that s^2_ijk gg fracsigma^2p^9/4polylog(p). On the other hand, under the same conditions, crefthm:asymptoticnormalityentries_v1 requires s^2_ijk to satisfy s^2_ijk gg fracsigma^2p^5/2 polylog(p), which is a factor of p^1/4 smaller than the condition in crefthm:civalidity_v1. However, this requirement still allows the appropriate rows of V_k to be a factor of p^1/8polylog(p) smaller than the maximum row norm. It may be possible to improve this result slightly by using a more refined analysis, but this is beyond the scope of this paper.

\label{cor:testing}
Consider the tensor mixed-membership model, where $r_k$ is fixed along each mode.  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item (Regularity) Each matricization of $\mathcal{S}$ has a bounded condition number.
\item (Identifiability) There is at least one pure node for each community along each mode.  
\item (Signal strength) The smallest singular value of $\mathcal{S}$ satisfies $\lambda_{\min}(\mathcal{S})^2/\sigma^2 \gg \frac{\log(p)}{p^{3/2}}.$
\item (Approximately equal community sizes) The community membership matrices $\mathbf{\Pi}_k$ satisfy $\lambda_{\min} \bigg( \mathbf{\Pi}_k^{\top} \mathbf{\Pi}_k \bigg) \gtrsim p.$
\end{itemize}
Then:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item (Consistency under the null) Under the null hypothesis $(\mathbf{\Pi}_k)_{i_k\cdot} = (\mathbf{\Pi}_k)_{i_k'\cdot}$, it holds that
    
    $\widehat T_{i_k i_k'} \to \chi^2_{r_k}$

in distribution as $p \to \infty$.
\item (Consistency against local alternatives) If it holds that $
    \frac{\lambda_{\min}(\mathcal{S}) p }{\sigma} \| \mathbf{\Pi}_{i_k\cdot} - \mathbf{\Pi}_{i_k'\cdot} \| \to \infty,$

then for any constant $C > 0$, 

$    \mathbb{P}( \widehat T_{i_k i_k'} > C ) \to 1.$

If instead, it holds that
\begin{align*}
    \big( ({\mathbf{U}}_k)_{i_k\cdot} - ({\mathbf{U}}_k)_{i_k'\cdot} \big)^{\top} \bigg( \mathbf{\Gamma}^{(i_k)}_k + \mathbf{\Gamma}^{(i_k')}_{k} \bigg)^{-1}\big(({\mathbf{U}}_k)_{i_k\cdot} - ({\mathbf{U}}_k)_{i_k'\cdot} \big) \to \gamma < \infty
\end{align*}
then 

$    \widehat T_{i_k i_k'} \to \chi^2(\gamma),$

as $p \to \infty$, where $\chi^2(\gamma)$ denotes a noncentral $\chi^2$ distribution with noncentrality parameter $\gamma$. 
\end{enumerate}

nodes.raw_latex:
In \cite{agterberg_estimating_2022}, the condition $\lambda_{\min}(\mathcal{S})^2/\sigma^2 \gtrsim \frac{\log(p)}{p^{3/2}}$ was shown to be sufficient for $\ell_{2,\infty}$ membership recovery when $r$ is fixed; our signal-strength condition is only slightly stronger than theirs.  




However, in contrast to \cite{agterberg_estimating_2022}, 
our results apply to testing whether two vertices have the same community memberships,  whereas \cite{agterberg_estimating_2022} focus only on estimation.

In addition, we assume that the membership matrices satisfy $\lambda_{\min}\big( \mathbf{\Pi}_k^{\top} \mathbf{\Pi}_k \big) \gtrsim p$. A similar condition was imposed in \cite{agterberg_estimating_2022}; implicitly this condition requires that the communities are approximately balanced.

In addition, we assume that the membership matrices satisfy lambda_minbig( Pi_k^top Pi_k big) gtrsim p. nodes.name: Comparison to  Matrix Two-Sample Testing
nodes.statement: Our result can also be compared to Theorem 1 of , where they prove (under a Bernoulli noise model), that their test statistic exhibits similar convergence in distribution (a similar result was obtained in ). Informally, their results demonstrate that sqrtp times SNR times \| Pi_icdot - Pi_jcdot \| to infty in order to achieve power converging to one, where their result holds for testing the i'th and j'th rows for a ptimes p symmetric matrix of the form Pi B Pi^top, and SNR denotes a measurement of the signal-to-noise ratio. In contrast, our results demonstrate that p times SNR times \| big(Pi_kbig)_i_k - big(Pi_kbig)_i_k' \| to infty is required in order to achieve power converging to one. Therefore our result yields an improvement of order sqrtp in the local power of our test statistic.

nodes.name: Signal Strength Condition
nodes.statement: The condition on s_min can be viewed as both a signal-strength requirement on the magnitudes of the corresponding entries of the rows of the V_k's as well as a condition governing how much the indices overlap, with more overlap requiring more minimum signal. Note that if J consists of |J| disjoint index sets, then the condition on s_min is comparable to the condition in crefthm:civalidity_v1 accounting for the size of the set J. If some terms share an index, then the condition on s_min governs how many terms can be shared.

nodes.raw_latex:
While the condition on $s_{\min}$ is hard to parse, consider the setting that $r = O(1)$, and that $\lambda/\sigma \asymp p^{3/4} {\rm polylog}(p)$.  Then our condition translates to the requirement
\begin{align*}
   s_{\min}/\sigma \gg \max\bigg\{  |J|^{3/2} \frac{1}{ p^{5/4} {\rm polylog}(p) }, |J| \frac{ 1}{p^{9/8} {\rm polylog}(p)},   |J|^{1/6} \frac{1}{p^{13/12}{\rm polylog}(p)}\bigg\},
\end{align*}
which demonstrates a tradeoff in the size of the index set $|J|$.  Consider the setting that $|J| = O(p^{1/6 - \varepsilon})$.  Then, ignoring logarithmic terms, this condition translates to the requirement 
$$s_{\min}/\sigma
     \gg \max\bigg\{ p^{-\varepsilon-23/24} , p^{-\varepsilon/6-19/18}\bigg\}$$




From this, we see that we need at least that $\varepsilon \geq \frac{1}{24}$ since the largest eigenvalue of $S_J/\sigma^2$ is of order at most $\frac{1}{p^2}$ by incoherence.  
However, as $\varepsilon$ increases (i.e., $|J|$ gets smaller), we see that we require less signal strength in each row of $\mathbf{V}_1$, $\mathbf{V}_2$, and $\mathbf{V}_3$.  Therefore, smaller index sets require less signal strength.

nodes.name: Index Overlap and Correlation
nodes.statement: crefthm:entrytesting_v1 demonstrates how the closeness of indices induces correlation via the additional correction terms required in widehat s^2_\ijk\\i'j'k'\ in crefal:entrytesting. For example, if one wishes to consider uncertainty quantification for the entries \i,j,k\ and \i',j,k\ simultaneously, the asymptotic variance in crefthm:entrytesting_v1 will have additional correlation since these two entries both share the indices j and k. Consequently, the closeness of indices corresponds to higher correlation, with the strength of correlation depending on how corresponding entries of right singular vectors interact.

Consequently, the closeness of indices corresponds to higher correlation, with the strength of correlation depending on how corresponding entries of right singular vectors interact.

\begin{align*}
    \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{Good}} &\coloneqq \bigg\{ \max_k \tau_k \leq C \sqrt{pr} \bigg\} \\
    &\qquad \bigcap \bigg\{ \| \sin\Theta(\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)}, {\mathbf{U}}_k ) \| \leq \frac{\delta_{\mathrm{L}}^{(k)}}{\lambda} + \frac{1}{2^{t}} \text{ for all $t \leq t_{\max}$ and $1\leq k \leq 3$ } \bigg\} \\
    &\qquad \bigcap \bigg\{ \max_k \bigg\| {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_k \mathbf{V}_k \bigg\| \leq C \left( \sqrt{r} + \sqrt{\log(p)} \right) \bigg\}; \\
    &\qquad \bigcap \bigg\{ \max_k  \bigg\| {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_k \mathcal{P}_{{\mathbf{U}}_{k+1}}  \otimes   \mathcal{P}_{{\mathbf{U}}_{k+2}}  \bigg\| \leq C \left( r + \sqrt{\log(p)} \right) \bigg\}; \\
    &\qquad \bigcap \bigg\{ \max_k \bigg\| \mathbf{Z}_k \mathbf{V}_k \bigg\| \leq C \sqrt{p_k} \bigg\}. \\
    \mathcal{E}_{2,\infty}^{t,k} &\coloneqq \bigg\{  \| \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)} - {\mathbf{U}}_k \mathbf{W}_k^{(t)} \|_{2,\infty} \leq \bigg( \frac{\delta_{\mathrm{L}}^{(k)}}{\lambda} + \frac{1}{2^{t}} \bigg) \mu_0 \sqrt{\frac{r_k}{p_k}} \bigg\}; \\
    
    \mathcal{E}_{j-m}^{t,k} &\coloneqq \bigg\{ \| \sin\Theta (\mathbf{\widetilde{U}}_k^{t,j-m}, \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)}) \| \leq  \bigg( \frac{\delta_{\mathrm{L}}^{(k)}}{\lambda} + \frac{1}{2^{t}} \bigg) \mu_0 \sqrt{\frac{r_k}{p_j}} \bigg\}; \\
    
  \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{main}}^{t_0-1,1} &\coloneqq \bigcap_{t=1}^{t_0-1} \Bigg\{ \bigcap_{k=1}^{3}  \mathcal{E}^{t,k}_{2,\infty} \cap  \bigcap_{j=1}^{3} \bigcap_{m=1}^{p_j} \mathcal{E}_{k-m}^{t,j} \Bigg\}; \\
       \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{main}}^{t_0-1,2} &\coloneqq\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{main}}^{t_0-1,1} \cap \bigg\{ \bigcap_{k=1}^{3} \bigcap_{m = 1}^{p_k} \mathcal{E}_{k-m}^{t_0,1} \bigg\} \cap \mathcal{E}_{2,\infty}^{t_0,1} \\
        \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{main}}^{t_0-1,3} &\coloneqq\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{main}}^{t_0-1,2} \cap \bigg\{ \bigcap_{k=1}^{3} \bigcap_{m = 1}^{p_k} \mathcal{E}_{k-m}^{t_0,2} \bigg\} \cap \mathcal{E}_{2,\infty}^{t_0,2}.\\
        \mathcal{\widetilde E}_{j-m}^{t,k} &\coloneqq \Bigg\{ \|\mathcal{\widetilde P}_k^{t_0,j-m}  \mathbf{V}_k \|_{2,\infty} \leq c \mu_0^2 \frac{\sqrt{r_{-k}}}{p_j} \bigg( \frac{\delta_{\mathrm{L}}^{(k+1)}}{\lambda} + \frac{1}{2^{t_0-1}}\bigg)\bigg( \frac{\delta_{\mathrm{L}}^{(k+2)}}{\lambda} + \frac{1}{2^{t_0-1}}\bigg) \\
     &\quad + c \mu_0^2 \frac{\sqrt{r_{-k}}}{\sqrt{p_jp_{k+2}}} \bigg( \frac{\delta_{\mathrm{L}}^{(k+1)}}{\lambda} + \frac{1}{2^{t_0-1}} \bigg) + c \mu_0^2 \frac{\sqrt{r_{-k}}}{\sqrt{p_j p_{k+1}}} \bigg( \frac{\delta_{\mathrm{L}}^{(k+2)}}{\lambda} + \frac{1}{2^{t_0-1}} \bigg)\\
     &\quad + c \mu_0^2 \frac{\sqrt{r_{-k}}}{\sqrt{p_{-k}}} \bigg( \frac{\delta_{\mathrm{L}}^{(k+1)}}{\lambda} + \frac{1}{2^{t_0-1}} \bigg) + c\mu_0^2 \frac{\sqrt{r_{-k}}}{\sqrt{p_{-k}}} \bigg( \frac{\delta_{\mathrm{L}}^{(k+2)}}{\lambda} + \frac{1}{2^{t_0-1}} \bigg) + c \mu_0 \sqrt{\frac{r_k}{p_{-k}}}.\Bigg\} \\
     &\bigcap \Bigg\{ \|\mathcal{\widetilde P}_k^{t_0,j-m}   \|_{2,\infty} \leq c \mu_0^2 \frac{\sqrt{r_{-k}}}{p_j}  \bigg( \frac{\delta_{\mathrm{L}}^{(k+1)}}{\lambda} + \frac{1}{2^{t_0-1}} \bigg)  \bigg( \frac{\delta_{\mathrm{L}}^{(k+2)}}{\lambda} + \frac{1}{2^{t_0-1}} \bigg) \\
    &\quad +  c\mu_0^2 \frac{\sqrt{r_{-k}}}{\sqrt{p_jp_{k+2}}} \bigg( \frac{\delta_{\mathrm{L}}^{(k+1)}}{\lambda} + \frac{1}{2^{t_0-1}} \bigg) + c\mu_0^2 \frac{\sqrt{r_{-k}}}{\sqrt{p_jp_{k+1}}} \bigg( \frac{\delta_{\mathrm{L}}^{(k+2)}}{\lambda} + \frac{1}{2^{t_0-1}} \bigg) + c\mu_0^2 \frac{\sqrt{r_{-k}}}{\sqrt{p_{-k}}}.\Bigg\},
  \end{align*}

As a result, letting widetilde Lambda_1^(t) denote the singular values of the matrix T_1 widehat P_1^(t), Weyl's inequality implies \| widetilde Lambda_1^(t) - widehat Lambda_1^(t) \| leq fraclambda8. Furthermore, since by definition T_1 = T_1 P_U_2 otimes U_3, we have that lambda_r_1 bigg( T_1 widehat P_1^(t) bigg) &= lambda_r_1 bigg( T_1P_U_2 otimes U_3 widehat P_1^(t) bigg) \\ &geq lambda_r_1bigg( T_1 U_2 otimes U_2 bigg) lambda_min bigg( big( U_2 otimes U_3 big)^top big( widehatU_3^(t-1) otimes widehatU_3^(t-1) big) bigg) \\ &= lambda_r_1 bigg( T_1 bigg) lambda_min big( U_2^top widehatU_2^(t) big) lambda_min big( U_3^top widehatU_3^(t) big). Next, by Lemma 1 of it holds that \| sinTheta(U_2, widehatU_2^(t))\|^2 &= 1 - lambda_minbig( U_2^top widehatU_2^(t) big)^2 which implies that lambda_minbig( U_2^top widehatU_2^(t) big) &= sqrt1 - \|sinTheta(U_2,widehatU_2^(t))\|^2 geq sqrt1 - frac1564 geq frac78, where we have used the fact that by , on the event E_Good one has \|sinTheta(U_2,widehatU_2^(t))\| lesssim fracdelta_Llambda leq frac38 leq sqrtfrac1564 since lambda gg delta_L = C_0 kappa sqrtplog(p) by assumption. nodes.raw_latex:
First, we note that with probability at least $1 - O(p^{-9})$ it holds that
\begin{align*}
    e_m^{\top} &\bigg( \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)} - {\mathbf{U}}_k \mathbf{W}_k^{(t)} \bigg) \\
    &\overset{\scalebox{.6}{\text{\cref{lem:linearapprox}}}}{=} e_m^{\top} (\mathbf{I} - {\mathbf{U}}_k {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} ) \mathbf{Z}_k \mathcal{\widehat P}_k^{(t)} \mathbf{V}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)} (\mathbf{\widehat{\Lambda}}_k^{(t)})^{-2}  \\
    &\qquad + O\bigg( \frac{\kappa \mu_0^2 r^{3/2}p \log(p)}{\lambda^3} + \frac{\mu_0^2 \big( r^2 \sqrt{\log(p)} + r \log(p)\big) + \mu_0 \kappa^2 \sqrt{pr} \log(p)}{\lambda^2} \bigg) \\
    &\overset{\scalebox{.6}{\text{\cref{uperplemma}}}}{=} e_m^{\top}  \mathbf{Z}_k \mathcal{\widehat P}_k^{(t)} \mathbf{V}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)} (\mathbf{\widehat{\Lambda}}_k^{(t)})^{-2}  \\
    &\qquad + O\bigg( \frac{\mu_0 r \kappa^2 \sqrt{p\log(p)}}{\lambda^2} + \frac{\mu_0 r \kappa}{\lambda \sqrt{p}} \bigg) \\
    &\quad + O\bigg( \frac{\kappa \mu_0^2 r^{3/2}p \log(p)}{\lambda^3} + \frac{\mu_0^2 \big( r^2 \sqrt{\log(p)} + r \log(p)\big) + \mu_0 \kappa^2 \sqrt{pr} \log(p)}{\lambda^2} \bigg) \\
    &\overset{\scalebox{.6}{\text{\cref{lem:empiricallinearreplacement}}}}{=} e_m^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_k \mathcal{ P}_k \mathbf{V}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)}  (\mathbf{\widehat{\Lambda}}_k^{(t)})^{-2} \\
    &\qquad + O\bigg( \frac{\kappa^2 \mu_0^2 \log(p) r \sqrt{p}}{\lambda^2} \bigg) \\
    &\qquad + O\bigg( \frac{\kappa \mu_0^2 r^{3/2}p \log(p)}{\lambda^3} + \frac{\mu_0^2 \big( r^2 \sqrt{\log(p)} + r \log(p)\big) + \mu_0 \kappa^2 \sqrt{pr} \log(p)}{\lambda^2} \bigg) \\
    &\qquad + O\bigg( \frac{\mu_0 r \kappa^2 \sqrt{p\log(p)}}{\lambda^2} + \frac{\mu_0 r \kappa}{\lambda \sqrt{p}} \bigg) \\
    &= e_m^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_k \mathbf{V}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^{-1} {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)} \\
    &\qquad + e_m^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_k \mathbf{V}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^{-1} \bigg( \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^2 {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)} - {\mathbf{U}}_k \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)} (\mathbf{\widehat{\Lambda}}_k^{(t)})^2 \bigg) (\mathbf{\widehat{\Lambda}}_k^{(t)})^{-2} \\
    &\qquad + O\bigg( \frac{\kappa^2 \mu_0^2 \log(p) r \sqrt{p}}{\lambda^2} \bigg) \\
    &\qquad + O\bigg( \frac{\kappa \mu_0^2 r^{3/2}p \log(p)}{\lambda^3} + \frac{\mu_0^2 \big( r^2 \sqrt{\log(p)} + r \log(p)\big) + \mu_0 \kappa^2 \sqrt{pr} \log(p)}{\lambda^2} \bigg) \\
    &\qquad + O\bigg( \frac{\mu_0 r \kappa^2 \sqrt{p\log(p)}}{\lambda^2} + \frac{\mu_0 r \kappa}{\lambda \sqrt{p}} \bigg) \\
    &= e_m^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_k \mathbf{V}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^{-1} \mathbf{W}_k^{(t)} + e_m^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_k \mathbf{V}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^{-1} \bigg( {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)} - \mathbf{W}_k^{(t)} \bigg) \\
    &\qquad + e_m^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_k \mathbf{V}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^{-1} \bigg( \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^2 {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)} - {\mathbf{U}}_k \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)} (\mathbf{\widehat{\Lambda}}_k^{(t)})^2 \bigg) (\mathbf{\widehat{\Lambda}}_k^{(t)})^{-2} \\
    &\qquad + O\bigg( \frac{\kappa^2 \mu_0^2 \log(p) r \sqrt{p}}{\lambda^2} \bigg) \\
    &\qquad + O\bigg( \frac{\kappa \mu_0^2 r^{3/2}p \log(p)}{\lambda^3} + \frac{\mu_0^2 \big( r^2 \sqrt{\log(p)} + r \log(p)\big) + \mu_0 \kappa^2 \sqrt{pr} \log(p)}{\lambda^2} \bigg) \\
     &\qquad + O\bigg( \frac{\mu_0 r \kappa^2 \sqrt{p\log(p)}}{\lambda^2} + \frac{\mu_0 r \kappa}{\lambda \sqrt{p}} \bigg).
\end{align*}
Note that by Lemma 16 of \cite{agterberg_estimating_2022} it holds that with probability at least $1 - O(p^{-30})$ that
\begin{align*}
    \| e_m^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_k \mathbf{V}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^{-1} \| &\lesssim p \sqrt{\log(p)} \| \mathbf{V}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^{-1} \|_{2,\infty} \\
    &\lesssim \frac{\mu_0 \sqrt{r\log(p)} }{\lambda}.
\end{align*}
\textcolor{black}{Furthermore, suppose ${\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)}$ has singular value decomposition  $\mathbf{W}_1 \mathbf{\Sigma} \mathbf{W}_2^{\top}$. 
 Then since $\mathbf{W}_k^{(t)} = \mathrm{sgn}({\mathbf{U}}_k, \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)})$, we have $\mathbf{W}_k^{(t)} = \mathbf{W}_1 \mathbf{W}_2^{\top}$, and $\mathbf{\Sigma}$ contains the diagonal entries equal to $\cos\theta_i$, with $\theta_i$ the canonical angles between the subspace spanned by ${\mathbf{U}}_k$ and $\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)}$ (see, e.g, \cite{kato2013perturbation}) and hence it holds that
\begin{align*}
    \| {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)} - \mathbf{W}_k^{(t)} \| &= \| \mathbf{W}_1 \mathbf{\Sigma} \mathbf{W}_2^{\top} - \mathbf{W}_1 \mathbf{W}_2^{\top} \| = \| \mathbf{\Sigma} - \mathbf{I} \| \\
    &= \max_{1\leq i \leq r} 1 - \cos\theta_i \leq \max_{1 \leq i\leq r} 1 - \cos^2 \theta_i = \max_{1\leq i \leq r} \sin^2\theta_i = \| \sin\Theta(\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)}, {\mathbf{U}}_k) \|^2.\addtocounter{equation}{1}\tag{\theequation} \label{sintheta14}
\end{align*}
}
Therefore, it holds on the event $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{Good}}$ that
\begin{align*}
    \| e_m^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_k \mathbf{V}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^{-1} \bigg( {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)} - \mathbf{W}_k^{(t)} \bigg) \| &\lesssim \frac{\mu_0 \sqrt{r\log(p)} }{\lambda} \| {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)} - \mathbf{W}_k^{(t)} \| \\
    &\lesssim\frac{\mu_0 \sqrt{r\log(p)} }{\lambda} \| \sin\Theta(\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)}, {\mathbf{U}}_k ) \|^2 \\
    &\overset{\scalebox{.6}{\text{\cref{sinthetaegood}}}}\lesssim \frac{\mu_0 \sqrt{r\log(p)} }{\lambda} \frac{\delta_{\mathrm{L}}^2}{\lambda^2} \\
    &\lesssim \frac{\mu_0 \kappa^2 p \sqrt{r} \log^{3/2}(p)  }{\lambda^3},
\end{align*}
and that
\begin{align*}
   \bigg\| e_m^{\top} &\mathbf{Z}_k \mathbf{V}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^{-1} \bigg( \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^2 {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)} - {\mathbf{U}}_k \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)} (\mathbf{\widehat{\Lambda}}_k^{(t)})^2 \bigg) (\mathbf{\widehat{\Lambda}}_k^{(t)})^{-2} \bigg\| \\&\lesssim \frac{\mu_0 \sqrt{r\log(p)} }{\lambda} \| \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^2 {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)} - {\mathbf{U}}_k \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)} (\mathbf{\widehat{\Lambda}}_k^{(t)})^2 \| \| (\mathbf{\widehat{\Lambda}}_k^{(t)})^{-2} \| \\
   &\overset{\scalebox{.6}{\text{\cref{lem:eigengaps}}}}{\lesssim} \frac{\mu_0 \sqrt{r\log(p)} }{\lambda^3} \| \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^2 {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)} - {\mathbf{U}}_k \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)} (\mathbf{\widehat{\Lambda}}_k^{(t)})^2 \| \\
   &\overset{\scalebox{.6}{\text{\cref{lem:approximatecommute}}}}{\lesssim} \frac{\mu_0 \sqrt{r\log(p)} }{\lambda^3} \lambda_1 \sqrt{pr} \\
   &\lesssim \frac{\mu_0 \kappa r \sqrt{p\log(p)} }{\lambda^2}.
\end{align*}
Therefore, we have shown that there is an event $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{Very Good}}$  with  $\mathbb{P}\big( \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{Very Good}}\big) \geq 1 - O(p^{-9})$ such that on this event
\begin{align*}
    e_m^{\top} &\bigg( \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)} - {\mathbf{U}}_k \mathbf{W}_k^{(t)} \bigg) \\
    &= e_m^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_k \mathbf{V}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^{-1} \mathbf{W}_k^{(t)} \\
    &\qquad + O\bigg( \frac{\mu_0 \kappa r \sqrt{p\log(p)} }{\lambda^2} + \frac{\mu_0 \kappa^2 p \sqrt{r} \log^{3/2}(p)  }{\lambda^3} \bigg) \\
    &\qquad + O\bigg( \frac{\kappa^2 \mu_0^2 \log(p) r \sqrt{p}}{\lambda^2} \bigg) \\
    &\qquad + O\bigg( \frac{\kappa \mu_0^2 r^{3/2}p \log(p)}{\lambda^3} + \frac{\mu_0^2 \big( r^2 \sqrt{\log(p)} + r \log(p)\big) + \mu_0 \kappa^2 \sqrt{pr} \log(p)}{\lambda^2} \bigg) \\ 
    &\qquad + O\bigg( \frac{\mu_0 r \kappa^2 \sqrt{p\log(p)}}{\lambda^2} + \frac{\mu_0 r \kappa}{\lambda \sqrt{p}} \bigg) \\
    &= e_m^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_k \mathbf{V}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^{-1} \mathbf{W}_k^{(t)} + O\bigg( \frac{\kappa^2 \mu_0^2 \log(p) r \sqrt{p}}{\lambda^2} + \frac{\mu_0 r \kappa}{\lambda \sqrt{p}} \bigg) 
\end{align*}
where we have used the fact that $\lambda \gtrsim \kappa \mu_0 \sqrt{pr \log(p)}$, which holds under the conditions of \cref{thm:eigenvectornormality} since $\mu_0^2 r \lesssim \sqrt{p}$. 
Therefore, by rotational invariance of vector norms, it holds that on this event
\begin{align*}
    e_m^{\top} \bigg( \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)} (\mathbf{W}_k^{(t)})^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_k \bigg) &= e_m^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_k \mathbf{V}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^{-1} + O\bigg( \frac{\kappa^2 \mu_0^2 \log(p) r \sqrt{p}}{\lambda^2} + \frac{\mu_0 r \kappa}{\lambda \sqrt{p}}  \bigg).
\end{align*}
This completes the proof.

nodes.statement: Again we assume that sigma = 1 without loss of generality. We suppress the dependence of widehatU_k^(t) and widehatLambda_k^(t) on t for convenience. Denoting W_k as the orthogonal matrix in crefthm:eigenvectornormality, by crefthm:eigenvectornormality on E_Theorem \ it holds that widehatU_k &widehatU_k^top - U_k U_k^top \\ &= widehatU_k (widehatU_k - U_k W_k )^top + (widehatU_k W_k^top - U_1)U_1^top \\ &= widehatU_k W_k^top (widehatU_k W_k^top - U_k )^top + (widehatU_k W_k^top - U_1)U_1^top \\ &= (widehatU_k W_k^top -U_k) (widehatU_k W_k^top - U_k )^top +U_k (widehatU_k W_k^top - U_k )^top+ (widehatU_k W_k^top - U_1)U_1^top \\ &= (Z_k V_k Lambda_k^-1 + Psi^(k)) (Z_k V_k Lambda_k^-1 + Psi^(k))^top \\ & +U_k (Z_k V_k Lambda_k^-1 + Psi^(k) )^top+ (Z_k V_k Lambda_k^-1 + Psi^(k))U_1^top \\ &= Z_k V_k Lambda_k^-2 V_k^top Z_k^top + Psi^(k) Lambda_k^-1 V_k^top Z_k^top + Z_k V_k Lambda_k^-1 (Psi^(k))^top + Psi^(k)(Psi^(k))^top\\ & + U_k Lambda_k^-1 V_k^top Z_k^top + U_k (Psi^(k))^top + Z_k V_k Lambda_k^-1 U_k^top + Psi^(k) U_k^top \\ &coloneqq U_k Lambda_k^-1 V_k^top Z_k^top + Z_k V_k Lambda_k^-1 U_k^top + Phi^(k). We now show the bound on Phi^(k) holds. We need to bound the terms Phi^(k)_1 &= Z_k V_k Lambda_k^-2 V_k^top Z_k^top; \\ Phi^(k)_2 &= Psi^(k)Lambda_k^-1 V_k^top Z_k^top; \\ Phi^(k)_3 &= Z_k V_k Lambda_k^-1(Psi^(k))^top; \\ Phi^(k)_4 &= Psi^(k) (Psi^(k))^top; \\ Phi^(k)_5 &= U_k (Psi^(k))^top; \\ Phi^(k)_6 &= Psi^(k) U_k^top. Note that by the proof of crefthm:eigenvectornormality it holds on E_Theorem \ that \| Z_k V_k Lambda_k^^-1 \|_2,infty &lesssim fracmu_0 sqrtrlog(p)lambda; \\ \| Z_k V_k \| &lesssim sqrtp, where the second inequality holds on the event E_Good (which is included implicitly in the event E_Theorem \ ). Therefore, \| Phi_1^(k) \|_2,infty &lesssim \| Z_k V_k Lambda_k^-1 \|_2,infty frac \| Z_k V_k \|lambda \\ &lesssim fracmu_0 sqrtrlog(p)lambda fracsqrtplambda \\ &lesssim frackappa^2 mu_0^2 log(p) r sqrtplambda^2. The second term can be bounded directly by noting that \| Phi_2^(k) \|_2,infty &leq \| Psi^(k) \|_2,infty \| Z_k V_k Lambda_k^-1 \| \\ &lesssim \| Psi^(k) \|_2,infty fracsqrtplambda \\ &ll \| Psi^(k) \|_2,infty \\ &lesssim frackappa^2 mu_0^2 log(p) r sqrtplambda^2. Next, \| Z_k V_k Lambda_k^-1 (Psi^(k))^top \|_2,infty &leq \| Z_k V_k Lambda_k^-1 \|_2,infty \| Psi^(k) \| \\ &lesssim fracmu_0 sqrtrlog(p)lambda sqrtp \| Psi^(k) \|_2,infty \\ &lesssim fracmu_0 sqrtrplog(p)lambda bigg( frac kappa^2 mu_0^2 log(p) r sqrtplambda^2 + fracmu_0 r kappalambda sqrtp bigg) \\ &lesssim frac kappa^2 mu_0^2 log(p) rsqrtplambda^2, since mu_0^2 r leq sqrtp and lambda gtrsim kappa p^3/4 sqrtlog(p). Next, \| Phi^(k)_4 \|_2,infty &= \| Psi^(k) (Psi^(k))^top \|_2,infty \\ &leq \| Psi^(k) \|_2,infty sqrtp \| Psi^(k)\|_2,infty \\ &lesssim bigg( frac kappa^2 mu_0^2 log(p) r sqrtplambda^2 + fracmu_0 r kappalambda sqrtp bigg) bigg( frac kappa^2 mu_0^2 log(p) r sqrtplambda^2 + fracmu_0 r kappalambda sqrtp bigg) sqrtp \\ &lesssim frac kappa^2 mu_0^2 log(p) rsqrtplambda^2. Next, \| Phi_5^(k) \|_2,infty &= \| U_k (Psi^(k))^top \|_2,infty \\ &leq \| U_k \|_2,infty \| Psi^(k) \| \\ &lesssim sqrtp \|U_k\|_2,infty \| Psi^(k) \|_2,infty \\ &lesssim mu_0 sqrtr \| Psi^(k) \|_2,infty \\ &lesssim mu_0 sqrtr bigg( frac kappa^2 mu_0^2 log(p) r sqrtplambda^2 + fracmu_0 r kappalambda sqrtp bigg) \\ &lesssim frackappa^2 mu_0^3 log(p) r^3/2 sqrtplambda^2 + fracmu_0^2 r^3/2 kappalambda sqrtp. The bound on \|Phi_6^(k)\|_2,infty holds from the same bound as \|Psi^(k)\|_2,infty, which completes the proof.
nodes.raw_latex:
Again we assume that $\sigma = 1$ without loss of generality. We suppress the dependence of $\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)}$ and $\mathbf{\widehat{\Lambda}}_k^{(t)}$ on $t$ for convenience.  Denoting $\mathbf{W}_k$ as the orthogonal matrix in \cref{thm:eigenvectornormality}, by \cref{thm:eigenvectornormality} on $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{Theorem} \ \ref{thm:eigenvectornormality}}$ it holds that
\begin{align*}
    \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k &\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_k {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} \\
    &= \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k - {\mathbf{U}}_k \mathbf{W}_k )^{\top} + (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k \mathbf{W}_k^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_1){\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top} \\
    &= \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k \mathbf{W}_k^{\top} (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k \mathbf{W}_k^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_k  )^{\top} + (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k \mathbf{W}_k^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_1){\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top} \\
    &= (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k \mathbf{W}_k^{\top} -{\mathbf{U}}_k) (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k \mathbf{W}_k^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_k  )^{\top} +{\mathbf{U}}_k (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k \mathbf{W}_k^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_k  )^{\top}+ (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k \mathbf{W}_k^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_1){\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top} \\
    &= (\mathbf{Z}_k \mathbf{V}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^{-1} + \mathbf{\Psi}^{(k)}) (\mathbf{Z}_k \mathbf{V}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^{-1} + \mathbf{\Psi}^{(k)})^{\top} \\
    &\quad +{\mathbf{U}}_k (\mathbf{Z}_k \mathbf{V}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^{-1} + \mathbf{\Psi}^{(k)}  )^{\top}+ (\mathbf{Z}_k \mathbf{V}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^{-1} + \mathbf{\Psi}^{(k)}){\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top} \\
    &= \mathbf{Z}_k \mathbf{V}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^{-2} \mathbf{V}_k^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_k^{\top} + \mathbf{\Psi}^{(k)} \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^{-1} \mathbf{V}_k^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_k^{\top} + \mathbf{Z}_k \mathbf{V}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^{-1} (\mathbf{\Psi}^{(k)})^{\top} + \mathbf{\Psi}^{(k)}(\mathbf{\Psi}^{(k)})^{\top}\\
    &\quad + {\mathbf{U}}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^{-1} \mathbf{V}_k^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_k^{\top} + {\mathbf{U}}_k (\mathbf{\Psi}^{(k)})^{\top}  + \mathbf{Z}_k \mathbf{V}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^{-1} {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} + \mathbf{\Psi}^{(k)} {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} \\
    &\coloneqq {\mathbf{U}}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^{-1} \mathbf{V}_k^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_k^{\top} + \mathbf{Z}_k \mathbf{V}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^{-1} {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} + \mathbf{\Phi}^{(k)}.
\end{align*}
We now show the bound on $\mathbf{\Phi}^{(k)}$ holds.  We need to bound the terms
\begin{align*}
    \mathbf{\Phi}^{(k)}_1 &= \mathbf{Z}_k \mathbf{V}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^{-2} \mathbf{V}_k^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_k^{\top}; \\
    \mathbf{\Phi}^{(k)}_2 &= \mathbf{\Psi}^{(k)}\mathbf{\Lambda}_k^{-1} \mathbf{V}_k^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_k^{\top}; \\
     \mathbf{\Phi}^{(k)}_3 &= \mathbf{Z}_k \mathbf{V}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^{-1}(\mathbf{\Psi}^{(k)})^{\top}; \\
      \mathbf{\Phi}^{(k)}_4 &= \mathbf{\Psi}^{(k)} (\mathbf{\Psi}^{(k)})^{\top}; \\
       \mathbf{\Phi}^{(k)}_5 &= {\mathbf{U}}_k (\mathbf{\Psi}^{(k)})^{\top}; \\
       \mathbf{\Phi}^{(k)}_6 &= \mathbf{\Psi}^{(k)} {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top}.
\end{align*}
Note that by the proof of \cref{thm:eigenvectornormality} it holds on $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{Theorem} \ \ref{thm:eigenvectornormality}}$ that
\begin{align*}
    \| \mathbf{Z}_k \mathbf{V}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^{^{-1}} \|_{2,\infty} &\lesssim \frac{\mu_0 \sqrt{r\log(p)}}{\lambda}; \\
    \| \mathbf{Z}_k \mathbf{V}_k \| &\lesssim \sqrt{p},
\end{align*}
where the second inequality holds on the event $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{Good}}$  (which is included implicitly in the event $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{Theorem} \ \ref{thm:eigenvectornormality}}$).  Therefore,
\begin{align*}
    \| \mathbf{\Phi}_1^{(k)} \|_{2,\infty} &\lesssim \| \mathbf{Z}_k \mathbf{V}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^{-1} \|_{2,\infty} \frac{ \| \mathbf{Z}_k \mathbf{V}_k \|}{\lambda} \\
    &\lesssim \frac{\mu_0 \sqrt{r\log(p)}}{\lambda} \frac{\sqrt{p}}{\lambda} \\
    &\lesssim \frac{\kappa^2 \mu_0^2 \log(p) r \sqrt{p}}{\lambda^2}.
\end{align*}
The second term can be bounded directly by noting that
\begin{align*}
    \| \mathbf{\Phi}_2^{(k)} \|_{2,\infty} &\leq \| \mathbf{\Psi}^{(k)} \|_{2,\infty} \| \mathbf{Z}_k \mathbf{V}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^{-1} \| \\
    &\lesssim \| \mathbf{\Psi}^{(k)} \|_{2,\infty} \frac{\sqrt{p}}{\lambda} \\
    &\ll \| \mathbf{\Psi}^{(k)} \|_{2,\infty} \\
    &\lesssim \frac{\kappa^2 \mu_0^2 \log(p) r \sqrt{p}}{\lambda^2}.
\end{align*}
Next,
\begin{align*}
    \| \mathbf{Z}_k \mathbf{V}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^{-1}  (\mathbf{\Psi}^{(k)})^{\top} \|_{2,\infty} &\leq   \| \mathbf{Z}_k \mathbf{V}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^{-1} \|_{2,\infty} \| \mathbf{\Psi}^{(k)} \| \\
    &\lesssim \frac{\mu_0 \sqrt{r\log(p)}}{\lambda} \sqrt{p} \| \mathbf{\Psi}^{(k)} \|_{2,\infty} \\
    &\lesssim \frac{\mu_0 \sqrt{rp\log(p)}}{\lambda} \bigg( \frac{ \kappa^2 \mu_0^2 \log(p) r \sqrt{p}}{\lambda^2} + \frac{\mu_0 r \kappa}{\lambda \sqrt{p}} \bigg) \\
   
    &\lesssim \frac{ \kappa^2 \mu_0^2 \log(p) r\sqrt{p}}{\lambda^2},
\end{align*}
since $\mu_0^2 r \leq \sqrt{p}$ and $\lambda \gtrsim \kappa p^{3/4} \sqrt{\log(p)}$.  Next,
\begin{align*}
    \| \mathbf{\Phi}^{(k)}_4 \|_{2,\infty} &= \| \mathbf{\Psi}^{(k)} (\mathbf{\Psi}^{(k)})^{\top} \|_{2,\infty} \\
    &\leq \| \mathbf{\Psi}^{(k)} \|_{2,\infty} \sqrt{p} \| \mathbf{\Psi}^{(k)}\|_{2,\infty} \\
    &\lesssim  \bigg( \frac{ \kappa^2 \mu_0^2 \log(p) r \sqrt{p}}{\lambda^2} + \frac{\mu_0 r \kappa}{\lambda \sqrt{p}} \bigg)  \bigg( \frac{ \kappa^2 \mu_0^2 \log(p) r \sqrt{p}}{\lambda^2} + \frac{\mu_0 r \kappa}{\lambda \sqrt{p}} \bigg) \sqrt{p} \\
    &\lesssim \frac{ \kappa^2 \mu_0^2 \log(p) r\sqrt{p}}{\lambda^2}.
\end{align*}
Next,
\begin{align*}
    \| \mathbf{\Phi}_5^{(k)} \|_{2,\infty} &= \| {\mathbf{U}}_k (\mathbf{\Psi}^{(k)})^{\top} \|_{2,\infty} \\
    &\leq \| {\mathbf{U}}_k \|_{2,\infty} \| \mathbf{\Psi}^{(k)} \| \\
    &\lesssim \sqrt{p} \|{\mathbf{U}}_k\|_{2,\infty} \| \mathbf{\Psi}^{(k)} \|_{2,\infty} \\
     &\lesssim \mu_0 \sqrt{r} \| \mathbf{\Psi}^{(k)} \|_{2,\infty} \\
     &\lesssim  \mu_0 \sqrt{r}  \bigg( \frac{ \kappa^2 \mu_0^2 \log(p) r \sqrt{p}}{\lambda^2} + \frac{\mu_0 r \kappa}{\lambda \sqrt{p}} \bigg) \\
     &\lesssim \frac{\kappa^2 \mu_0^3 \log(p) r^{3/2} \sqrt{p}}{\lambda^2}   + \frac{\mu_0^2 r^{3/2} \kappa}{\lambda \sqrt{p}}.
     
\end{align*}
The bound on $\|\mathbf{\Phi}_6^{(k)}\|_{2,\infty}$ holds from the same bound as $\|\mathbf{\Psi}^{(k)}\|_{2,\infty}$, which completes the proof.

\begin{align*}

    &\leq \| {\mathbf{U}}_k \|_{2\infty} \| \mathbf{\Lambda}_k \| \|(\mathbf{\widehat \Lambda}_k^{(t)})^{-2} \| \bigg( \| {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_k \big( \mathcal{P}_k -\mathcal{\widehat P}_k^{(t)} \big) \mathbf{V}_k \| + \| {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_k \mathbf{V}_k \|  \bigg)\\
    &\lesssim \mu_0 \sqrt{\frac{r}{p}} \frac{\kappa}{\lambda} \bigg( \| {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_k \big( \mathcal{P}_k -\mathcal{\widehat P}_k^{(t)} \big) \mathbf{V}_k \| + \| {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_k \mathbf{V}_k \|  \bigg) \\
    &\lesssim \mu_0 \sqrt{\frac{r}{p}} \frac{\kappa}{\lambda} \bigg( \| \mathbf{Z}_k \big( \mathcal{P}_{{\mathbf{U}}_{k+1}} \otimes \mathcal{P}_{{\mathbf{U}}_{k+2}}  -\mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_{k+1}^{(t)}} \otimes \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_{k+2}^{(t)}}  \big)  \| + \sqrt{r} \bigg) \\
    &\lesssim \mu_0 \sqrt{\frac{r}{p}} \frac{\kappa}{\lambda} \bigg( \sqrt{rp} \frac{\kappa \sqrt{p\log(p)}}{\lambda} + \sqrt{r} \bigg)  \\
    &\asymp \frac{\mu_0 r \kappa^2 \sqrt{p\log(p)}}{\lambda^2} + \frac{\mu_0 r \kappa}{\lambda \sqrt{p}},
\end{align*}
where we have implicitly used the fact that
\begin{align*}
    \| \mathbf{Z}_k \big(& \mathcal{P}_{{\mathbf{U}}_{k+1}} \otimes \mathcal{P}_{{\mathbf{U}}_{k+2}}  -\mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_{k+1}^{(t)}} \otimes \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_{k+2}^{(t)}}  \big)  \|\\
    &\leq  \| \mathbf{Z}_k \big( \mathcal{P}_{{\mathbf{U}}_{k+1}} \otimes \bigg( \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widehat{U}}^{(t)}_{k+2}}  - \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_{k+2}^{(t)}}  \bigg)   \| + \| \mathbf{Z}_k \bigg( \mathcal{P}_{{\mathbf{U}}_{k+1}} - \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widehat{U}}^{(t)}_{k+1}} \bigg) \otimes  \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widehat{U}}^{(t)}_{k+2}} \| \\

    &\lesssim \sqrt{pr} \frac{\kappa \sqrt{p\log(p)}}{\lambda},

Without loss of generality, we consider $k = 1$.  On the event $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{Good}} \cap \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{main}}^{t,1}$, it holds that
\begin{align*}
    \bigg\| e_m^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_1 \bigg( \mathcal{\widehat P}_1^{(t)} -  \mathcal{P}_1 \bigg) \mathbf{V}_1 \mathbf{\Lambda}_1 {\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top} \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1^{(t)}  (\mathbf{\widehat\Lambda}_1^{(t)})^{-2} \bigg\| &\lesssim \frac{\kappa}{\lambda} \bigg\| e_m^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_1 \bigg( \mathcal{\widetilde P}_{1}^{t,1-m} - \mathcal{\widehat P}_1^{(t)} \bigg) \mathbf{V}_k \bigg\| \\
    &\qquad + \frac{\kappa}{\lambda} \bigg\| e_m^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_1 \bigg( \mathcal{\widetilde P}_{1}^{t,1-m} - \mathcal{ P}_1 \bigg) \mathbf{V}_k \bigg\| \\
    &\coloneqq (I) + (II).
\end{align*}
For term $(I)$, we note that
\begin{align*}
    (I) &= \frac{\kappa}{\lambda} \bigg\| e_m^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_1 \bigg( \mathcal{\widetilde P}_{1}^{t,1-m} - \mathcal{\widehat P}_1^{(t)} \bigg) \mathbf{V}_k \bigg\| \\
    &= \frac{\kappa}{\lambda} \bigg\| e_m^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_1 \bigg( \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widetilde{U}}_2^{(t-1,1-m)}} \otimes \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widetilde{U}}_3^{(t-1,1-m)}} - \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2^{(t-1)}} \otimes \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_3^{(t-1)}} \bigg) \mathbf{V}_k \bigg\| \\
    &\leq \frac{\kappa}{\lambda} \bigg\| e_m^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_1 \bigg( \bigg[\mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widetilde{U}}_2}^{(t-1,1-m)} - \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2^{(t-1)}} \bigg] \otimes \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_3^{(t-1)}} \bigg) \mathbf{V}_k \bigg\| \\
    &\qquad + \frac{\kappa}{\lambda} \bigg\| e_m^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_1 \bigg( \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widetilde{U}}_2}^{(t-1,1-m)} \otimes \bigg[  \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widetilde{U}}_3^{(t-1,1-m)}} -  \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_3^{(t-1)}} \bigg]\bigg) \mathbf{V}_k \bigg\| \\
    &\lesssim \frac{\kappa \tau_k}{\lambda}  \bigg(\| \sin\Theta(\mathbf{\widetilde{U}}_2^{(t-1,1-m)},\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2^{(t-1)}) \|  + \| \sin\Theta(\mathbf{\widetilde{U}}_3^{(t-1,1-m)},\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_3^{(t-1)}) \| \bigg) \\
    &\overset{\scalebox{.6}{\text{\cref{sinthetaloo14}}}}{\lesssim} \frac{\kappa \sqrt{pr}}{\lambda} \frac{\delta_{\mathrm{L}}}{\lambda} \mu_0 \sqrt{\frac{r}{p}}\\
    &\lesssim \frac{ \mu_0 \kappa^2 r \sqrt{p\log(p)}}{\lambda^2},
\end{align*}
where the penultimate bound holds on the event $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{main}}^{t_0,1}$.  
Similarly, for term $(II)$, by Lemma 16 of \cite{agterberg_estimating_2022}, it holds that with probability at least $1 - O(p^{-30})$ that
\begin{align*}
    (II) &=  \frac{\kappa}{\lambda} \bigg\| e_m^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_1 \bigg( \mathcal{\widetilde P}_{1}^{t,1-m} - \mathcal{ P}_1 \bigg) \mathbf{V}_k \bigg\| \\
    &\lesssim \frac{\kappa}{\lambda} p \sqrt{\log(p)} \bigg\| \bigg( \mathcal{\widetilde P}_{1}^{t,1-m} - \mathcal{ P}_1 \bigg) \mathbf{V}_k \bigg\|_{2,\infty}.
\end{align*}
We now observe that
\begin{align*}
    \| \bigg( \mathcal{\widetilde P}_1^{t,1-m} - \mathcal{P}_1 \bigg) \mathbf{V}_k \bigg\|_{2,\infty} &=  \bigg\| \bigg( \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widetilde{U}}_2^{(t-1,1-m)}} \otimes \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widetilde{U}}_3^{(t-1,1-m)}} - \mathcal{P}_{{\mathbf{U}}_2} \otimes \mathcal{P}_{{\mathbf{U}}_3} \bigg) \mathbf{V}_k \bigg\|_{2,\infty}  \\
    &\leq \bigg\| \bigg( \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widetilde{U}}_2^{(t-1,1-m)}} \otimes \bigg[ \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widetilde{U}}_3^{(t-1,1-m)}} - \mathcal{P}_{{\mathbf{U}}_3} \bigg]\bigg) \mathbf{V}_k \bigg\|_{2,\infty}  \\
    &\qquad + \bigg\| \bigg(\bigg[ \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widetilde{U}}_2^{(t-1,1-m)}} - \mathcal{P}_{{\mathbf{U}}_2} \bigg] \otimes  \mathcal{P}_{{\mathbf{U}}_3} \bigg] \bigg) \mathbf{V}_k \bigg\|_{2,\infty} \\
    &\leq \| \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widetilde{U}}_2^{(t-1,1-m)}} \|_{2,\infty} \| \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widetilde{U}}_3^{(t-1,1-m)}} - \mathcal{P}_{{\mathbf{U}}_3} \|_{2,\infty} \\
    &\qquad + \| \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widetilde{U}}_2^{(t-1,1-m)}} - \mathcal{P}_{{\mathbf{U}}_2} \|_{2,\infty}  \mu_0 \sqrt{\frac{r}{p}} \\
    &\leq \| \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widetilde{U}}_2^{(t-1,1-m)}} - \mathcal{P}_{{\mathbf{U}}_2} \|_{2,\infty} \| \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widetilde{U}}_3^{(t-1,1-m)}} - \mathcal{P}_{{\mathbf{U}}_3} \|_{2,\infty} \\
    &\qquad + \| \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widetilde{U}}_3^{(t-1,1-m)}} - \mathcal{P}_{{\mathbf{U}}_3} \|_{2,\infty} \mu_0 \sqrt{\frac{r}{p}} \\
    &\qquad + \| \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widetilde{U}}_2^{(t-1,1-m)}} - \mathcal{P}_{{\mathbf{U}}_2} \|_{2,\infty}  \mu_0 \sqrt{\frac{r}{p}}.
\end{align*}
It is straightforward to check that
\begin{align*}
    \| \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widetilde{U}}_2^{(t-1,1-m)}} - \mathcal{P}_{{\mathbf{U}}_2} \|_{2,\infty} &\leq \|  \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widetilde{U}}_2^{(t-1,1-m)}} - \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2^{(t-1)}} \|_{2,\infty} + \| \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2^{(t-1)}}  - \mathcal{P}_{{\mathbf{U}}_2}\|_{2,\infty} \\
    &\lesssim \|\sin\Theta(\mathbf{\widetilde{U}}_2^{(t-1,1-m)},\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2^{(t-1)} ) \| \\
    &\quad + \| {\mathbf{U}}_2 \|_{2,\infty} \|\sin\Theta(\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2^{(t-1)},{\mathbf{U}}_2) \| + \| \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2^{(t-1)} - {\mathbf{U}}_2 \mathbf{W}_2^{(t-1)} \|_{2,\infty} \\
    &\lesssim \mu_0 \sqrt{\frac{r}{p}} \frac{\delta_{\mathrm{L}}}{\lambda},
\end{align*}
where the final bound holds on the event \textcolor{black}{$\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{main}}^{t_0,1} \cap \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{Good}}$ by \cref{sinthetaloo14,sinthetaegood}}.  
The same bounds holds with $\mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widetilde{U}}_3^{(t-1,1-m)}}$ in place of $\mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widetilde{U}}_2^{(t-1,1-m)}}$.  Plugging this bound in yields that with probability at least $1 - O(p^{-11})$,
\begin{align*}
    (II)  &\lesssim \frac{\kappa}{\lambda} p \sqrt{\log(p)} \bigg\| \bigg( \mathcal{\widetilde P}_{1}^{t,1-m} - \mathcal{ P}_1 \bigg) \mathbf{V}_k \bigg\|_{2,\infty} \\
    &\lesssim \frac{\kappa}{\lambda} p \sqrt{\log(p)} \bigg( \| \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widetilde{U}}_2^{(t-1,1-m)}} - \mathcal{P}_{{\mathbf{U}}_2} \|_{2,\infty} \| \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widetilde{U}}_3^{(t-1,1-m)}} - \mathcal{P}_{{\mathbf{U}}_3} \|_{2,\infty} \\
    &\qquad + \| \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widetilde{U}}_3^{(t-1,1-m)}} - \mathcal{P}_{{\mathbf{U}}_3} \|_{2,\infty} \mu_0 \sqrt{\frac{r}{p}} \\
    &\qquad + \| \mathcal{P}_{\mathbf{\widetilde{U}}_2^{(t-1,1-m)}} - \mathcal{P}_{{\mathbf{U}}_2} \|_{2,\infty}  \mu_0 \sqrt{\frac{r}{p}} \bigg) \\
    &\lesssim \frac{\kappa}{\lambda} p \sqrt{\log(p)} \bigg( \mu_0^2 \frac{r}{p} \frac{\delta_{\mathrm{L}}}{\lambda} \bigg) \\
    &\lesssim \frac{\kappa^2 \mu_0^2 \log(p) r \sqrt{p}}{\lambda^2}.
\end{align*}
Combining our bounds for both $(I)$ and $(II)$, we obtain that
\begin{align*}
    (I) + (II) &\lesssim \frac{\mu_0 \kappa^2 r \sqrt{p\log(p)}}{\lambda^2} + \frac{\kappa^2 \mu_0^2 \log(p) r \sqrt{p}}{\lambda^2} \\
    &\asymp \frac{\kappa^2 \mu_0^2 \log(p) r \sqrt{p}}{\lambda^2}.
\end{align*}
These bounds hold cumulatively with probability at most $1 - O(p^{-10})$, and the proof is completed by taking a union bound over all $p_1$ rows.

First, by the eigenvector-eigenvalue equation, it holds that
\begin{align*}
    {\mathbf{U}}_k \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^2 &= \mathbf{T}_k \mathbf{T}_k^{\top} {\mathbf{U}}_k; \\
    \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k (\mathbf{\widehat \Lambda}_k^{(t)} )^2 &= \bigg( \mathbf{T}_k \mathcal{\widehat P}_k^{(t)} \mathbf{T}_k^{\top} + \mathbf{Z}_k \mathcal{\widehat P}_k^{(t)} \mathbf{T}_k^{\top} +\mathbf{T}_k\mathcal{\widehat P}_k^{(t)} \mathbf{Z}_k^{\top} +\mathbf{Z}_k\mathcal{\widehat P}_k^{(t)} \mathbf{Z}_k^{\top} \bigg) \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k.
\end{align*}
Therefore,
\begin{align*}
    \bigg\| \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^2& {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k - {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k (\mathbf{\widehat\Lambda}_k^{(t)})^2 \bigg\|\\
    &=   \bigg\| {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top}\bigg( \mathbf{T}_k \mathbf{T}_k^{\top} - \mathbf{T}_k \mathcal{\widehat P}_k^{(t)} \mathbf{T}_k^{\top} - \mathbf{Z}_k \mathcal{\widehat P}_k^{(t)} \mathbf{T}_k^{\top} -\mathbf{T}_k\mathcal{\widehat P}_k^{(t)} \mathbf{Z}_k^{\top} -\mathbf{Z}_k\mathcal{\widehat P}_k^{(t)} \mathbf{Z}_k^{\top} \bigg) \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k \bigg\|
    \\
    &\leq +     \bigg\| {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} \bigg( \mathbf{T}_k \mathbf{T}_k^{\top} - \mathbf{T}_k \mathcal{\widehat P}_k^{(t)} \mathbf{T}_k^{\top} \bigg) \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k \bigg\|
    \\
    &\quad +  \bigg\| {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} \bigg( \mathbf{Z}_k \mathcal{\widehat P}_k^{(t)} \mathbf{T}_k^{\top} + \mathbf{T}_k \mathcal{\widehat P}_k^{(t)} \mathbf{Z}_k^{\top} + \mathbf{Z}_k \mathcal{\widehat P}_k^{(t)} \mathbf{Z}_k^{\top} \bigg) \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)} \bigg\| \\
    &\leq \bigg\| {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} \mathbf{T}_k \bigg( \mathcal{P}_{{\mathbf{U}}_{k+1} \otimes {\mathbf{U}}_{k+2}} - \mathcal{\widehat P}_k^{(t)} \bigg) \mathbf{T}_k^{\top} \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k \bigg\| \\
    &\quad + \bigg\| {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_k \mathcal{\widehat P}_k^{(t)} \mathbf{T}_k^{\top} \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)} \bigg\| + \bigg\| {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} \mathbf{T}_k \mathcal{\widehat P}_k^{(t)} \mathbf{Z}_k^{\top} \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)} \bigg\| + \bigg\| {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_k \mathcal{\widehat P}_k^{(t)} \mathbf{Z}_k^{\top} \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{(t)} \bigg\| \\
    &\lesssim \lambda_1^2 \frac{\kappa \sqrt{p\log(p)}}{\lambda} + \lambda_1 \tau_k + \tau_k^2 \\
    &\lesssim \kappa^2 \sqrt{p\log(p)} + \lambda_1 \sqrt{pr} \\
    &\lesssim \lambda_1 \sqrt{pr},
\end{align*}
where the final inequality holds when $\lambda_1 \gtrsim \sqrt{p\log(p)}$ together with the assumption that $\kappa \leq p^{1/4}$.  \textcolor{black}{In addition, we have implicitly used the bound
\begin{align*}
    \| \mathcal{P}_{{\mathbf{U}_{k+1}\otimes {\mathbf{U}}_{k+2}}} - \mathcal{\widehat P}_k^{(t)} \| \leq \| \sin\Theta(\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_{k+1}^{(t)},{\mathbf{U}}_{k+1}) \| + \| \sin\Theta(\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_{k+2}^{(t)},{\mathbf{U}}_{k+2})\| 
    &\lesssim \frac{\delta_{\mathrm{L}}}{\lambda},
\end{align*}
which holds on the event $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{Good}}$ by \eqref{sinthetaegood}.
}

     &\lesssim  \frac{\sigma^2 \mu_0^3 r^{3/2} \log(p)}{\lambda \sqrt{p}}; \\
     \bigg| \bigg(& \mathcal{Z} \times_1 (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_1 {\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top}) \times_2 (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_1 {\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top}) \times_3 (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_3 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_3^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top}) \bigg)_{ijk} \bigg| \\&\lesssim  \frac{\sigma^2 \mu_0^3 r^{3/2} \log(p)}{\lambda \sqrt{p}}.
\end{align*}

   &\quad + \bigg( \mathcal{T} \times_1 (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_1{\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top}) \times_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top} \times_3 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_3\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_3^{\top} \bigg)_{ijk} \\
   &\quad + \bigg( \mathcal{T} \times_1  {\mathbf{U}}_1{\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top} \times_2 (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top}) \times_3 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_3\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_3^{\top} \bigg)_{ijk} \\
    &\quad + \bigg( \mathcal{T} \times_1  {\mathbf{U}}_1{\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top} \times_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top} \times_3 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_3\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_3^{\top} \bigg)_{ijk} \\
    
    &= \bigg( \mathcal{T} \times_1 (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_1{\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top}) \times_2 ( \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top}) \times_3 (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_3\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_3^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top}) \bigg)_{ijk} \\
    &\quad + \bigg( \mathcal{T} \times_1 (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_1{\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top}) \times_2 ( \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top}) \times_3 ({\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top}) \bigg)_{ijk} \\
   &\quad + \bigg( \mathcal{T} \times_1 (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_1{\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top}) \times_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top} \times_3 (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_3\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_3^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top})\bigg)_{ijk} \\
   &\quad + \bigg( \mathcal{T} \times_1 (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_1{\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top}) \times_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top} \times_3 ( {\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top})\bigg)_{ijk} \\
   &\quad + \bigg( \mathcal{T} \times_1  {\mathbf{U}}_1{\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top} \times_2 (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top}) \times_3 (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_3\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_3^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top}) \bigg)_{ijk} \\
   &\quad + \bigg( \mathcal{T} \times_1  {\mathbf{U}}_1{\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top} \times_2 (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top}) \times_3 ( {\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top}) \bigg)_{ijk} \\
    &\quad + \bigg( \mathcal{T} \times_1  {\mathbf{U}}_1{\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top} \times_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top} \times_3 (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_3\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_3^{\top}  - {\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top})\bigg)_{ijk} \\
    &\quad + \bigg( \mathcal{T} \times_1  {\mathbf{U}}_1{\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top} \times_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top} \times_3  {\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top} \bigg)_{ijk}.
\end{align*}
The final term is simply $\mathcal{T}_{ijk}$. Similar to the previous case, the terms appearing all appear with either ${\mathbf{U}}_k {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top}$ or the difference $\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_k {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top}$.  We will show that terms with at least two projection-norm differences are small-order terms. Again, since $r_k \asymp r$ and $p_k \asymp p$, it suffices to analyze the two terms
\begin{align*}
    (I) &\coloneqq  \bigg( \mathcal{T} \times_1 (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_1{\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top}) \times_2 ( \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top}) \times_3 ({\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top}) \bigg)_{ijk}; \\
    (II) &\coloneqq \bigg( \mathcal{T} \times_1 (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_1{\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top}) \times_2 ( \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top}) \times_3 (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_3 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_3^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top}) \bigg)_{ijk}.
\end{align*}
By \cref{lem:tentrywiselemma}, it holds with probability at least $1 - O(p^{-9})$ that
\begin{align*}
    (I) + (II) &\lesssim \frac{\sigma^2 \mu_0^3 r^{3/2} \kappa \log(p)}{\lambda \sqrt{p}}.
\end{align*}
By symmetry, we have shown so far that with probability at least $1 - O(p^{-9})$,
\begin{align*}
    \mathcal{\widehat T}_{ijk} - \mathcal{T}_{ijk} &=  \bigg( \mathcal{T} \times_1 (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_1{\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top}) \times_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top} \times_3 ( {\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top})\bigg)_{ijk} \\
    &\quad +  \bigg( \mathcal{T} \times_1  {\mathbf{U}}_1{\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top} \times_2 (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top}) \times_3 ( {\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top}) \bigg)_{ijk} \\
    &\quad + \bigg( \mathcal{T} \times_1  {\mathbf{U}}_1{\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top} \times_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top} \times_3 (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_3\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_3^{\top}  - {\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top})\bigg)_{ijk} \\
    &\quad + O\bigg( \sigma \mu_0^3 \sqrt{\log(p)} \frac{r^{3/2}}{p^{3/2}} \bigg) \\
    &\quad + O\bigg( \frac{\sigma^2 \mu_0^3 r^{3/2} \kappa \log(p)}{\lambda \sqrt{p}} \bigg).
\end{align*}
We will now argue that the difference terms consist of another leading-order term.  More specifically, considering $k=1$, we will show that
\begin{align*}
    \bigg( \mathcal{T} \times_1 (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_1{\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top}) \times_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top} \times_3 ( {\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top})\bigg)_{ijk} &= e_i^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_1 \mathbf{V}_1 \mathbf{V}_1^{\top} e_{(j-1)p_3 + k} + o( s_{ijk}).
\end{align*}
The other indices will follow by symmetry.  

By \cref{cor:asymptoticnormality_projection} on the event $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{\cref{thm:eigenvectornormality}}}$ it holds that
\begin{align*}
     \bigg( \mathcal{T} \times_1 &(\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_1{\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top}) \times_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top} \times_3 ( {\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top})\bigg)_{ijk} \\
     &=  \bigg( \mathcal{T} \times_1 (\mathbf{U}_1 \mathbf{\Lambda}_1^{-1} \mathbf{V}_1 \mathbf{Z}_1^{\top} + \mathbf{Z}_1 \mathbf{V}_1 \mathbf{\Lambda}_1^{-1} {\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top} + \mathbf{\Phi}^{(1)}) \times_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top} \times_3 ( {\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top})\bigg)_{ijk} \\
     &= \bigg( \mathcal{T} \times_1 (\mathbf{U}_1 \mathbf{\Lambda}_1^{-1} \mathbf{V}_1 \mathbf{Z}_1^{\top} ) \times_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top} \times_3 ( {\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top})\bigg)_{ijk}  \\
     &\quad +\bigg( \mathcal{T} \times_1 ( \mathbf{Z}_1 \mathbf{V}_1 \mathbf{\Lambda}_1^{-1} {\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top} ) \times_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top} \times_3 ( {\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top})\bigg)_{ijk} \\
     &\quad +\bigg( \mathcal{T} \times_1 ( \mathbf{\Phi}^{(1)}) \times_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top} \times_3 ( {\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top})\bigg)_{ijk}.
\end{align*}
The first term satisfies
\begin{align*}
    \bigg( \mathcal{T} &\times_1 ( {\mathbf{U}}_1 \mathbf{\Lambda}_1^{-1} \mathbf{V}_1 \mathbf{Z}_1^{\top}) \times_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top} \times_3 ( {\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top})\bigg)_{ijk} \\
    &= \mathcal{M}_1 \bigg( \mathcal{T} \times_1 ( {\mathbf{U}}_1 \mathbf{\Lambda}_1^{-1} \mathbf{V}_1 \mathbf{Z}_1^{\top}) \times_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top} \times_3 ( {\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top} ) \bigg)_{i, (j-1)p_3 + k} \\
    &= e_i^{\top} \mathcal{M}_1 \bigg( \mathcal{T} \times_1 ( {\mathbf{U}}_1 \mathbf{\Lambda}_1^{-1} \mathbf{V}_1 \mathbf{Z}_1^{\top}) \bigg) ( {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top} \otimes {\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top} ) e_{(j-1)p_3 + k} \\
    &= e_i^{\top} {\mathbf{U}}_1 \mathbf{\Lambda}_1^{-1} \mathbf{V}_1 \mathbf{Z}_1^{\top} \mathbf{T}_1 ( {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top} \otimes {\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top} ) e_{(j-1)p_3 + k} \\
    &= e_i^{\top} {\mathbf{U}}_1 \mathbf{\Lambda}_1^{-1} \mathbf{V}_1 \mathbf{Z}_1^{\top} {\mathbf{U}}_1 \mathbf{\Lambda}_1 \mathbf{V}_1^{\top} e_{(j-1)p_3 + k}.
\end{align*}
On the event $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{VeryGood}}$ it holds that
\begin{align*}
    \|{\mathbf{U}}_1 ^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_1 \mathbf{V}_1 \| &\lesssim \sigma \sqrt{r}.
\end{align*}
Therefore, on this event,
\begin{align*}
    | e_i^{\top} {\mathbf{U}}_1 \mathbf{\Lambda}_1^{-1} \mathbf{V}_1 \mathbf{Z}_1^{\top} {\mathbf{U}}_1 \mathbf{\Lambda}_1 \mathbf{V}_1^{\top} e_{(j-1)p_3 + k} | &\leq \kappa \| e_i^{\top} {\mathbf{U}}_1 \| \| e_{(j-1)p_3 + k}^{\top} \mathbf{V}_1 \| \|{\mathbf{U}}_1 ^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_1 \mathbf{V}_1 \| \\
    &\lesssim \kappa \sigma \mu_0^2 \frac{r^{3/2}}{p^{3/2}}.
\end{align*}
In addition,
\begin{align*}
   | \bigg( \mathcal{T} &\times_1 ( \mathbf{\Phi}^{(1)}) \times_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top} \times_3 ( {\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top})\bigg)_{ijk} |\\
   &= | e_i^{\top} \mathbf{\Phi}^{(1)} \mathbf{T}_1 ({\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top} \otimes {\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top}) e_{(j-1)p_3 + k} | \\
   &\leq \| e_i^{\top} \mathbf{\Phi}^{(1)} \| \| \mathbf{T}_1 e_{(j-1)p_3 + k} \| \\
   &\leq \| \mathbf{\Phi}^{(1)} \|_{2,\infty} \| \mathbf{T}_1^{\top} \|_{2,\infty}  \\
   &\lesssim \bigg(  \frac{\sigma^2 \kappa^2 \mu_0^3 \log(p) r^{3/2} \sqrt{p}}{\lambda^2} + \frac{\sigma \mu_0^2 r^{3/2} \kappa}{\lambda \sqrt{p}}  \bigg)\lambda_1 \mu_0 \frac{\sqrt{r}}{p} \\
   &\lesssim 
   \frac{\kappa^3 \sigma^2 \mu_0^4 \log(p) r^2}{\lambda \sqrt{p}} + \frac{\kappa^2 \mu_0^3 r^2 \sigma}{ p^{3/2}}
\end{align*}
The remaining term satisfies
\begin{align*}
    \bigg( \mathcal{T} &\times_1 ( \mathbf{Z}_1 \mathbf{V}_1 \mathbf{\Lambda}_1^{-1} {\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top} ) \times_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top} \times_3 ( {\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top})\bigg)_{ijk} \\
    &= e_i^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_1 \mathbf{V}_1 \mathbf{\Lambda}_1^{-1} {\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top} \mathbf{T}_1 ( {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top} \otimes {\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top} ) e_{(j-1)p_3 + k} \\
    &= e_i^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_1 \mathbf{V}_1 \mathbf{\Lambda}_1^{-1} {\mathbf{U}}_1 ^{\top} {\mathbf{U}}_1 \mathbf{\Lambda}_1 \mathbf{V}_1^{\top}  e_{(j-1)p_3 + k} \\
    &= e_i^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_1 \mathbf{V}_1 \mathbf{V}_1^{\top}  e_{(j-1)p_3 + k}.
\end{align*}
Therefore, we have shown that with probability at least $1 - O(p^{-9})$,
\begin{align*}
    \bigg( \mathcal{T}& \times_1 (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_1{\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top}) \times_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top} \times_3 ( {\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top})\bigg)_{ijk} \\
    &= e_i^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_1 \mathbf{V}_1 \mathbf{V}_1^{\top}  e_{(j-1)p_3 + k} \\
    &\quad + O\bigg( \frac{\kappa^2 \sigma \mu_0^3 r^{2}}{p^{3/2}} + \frac{\kappa^3 \sigma^2 \mu_0^4 \log(p) r^2}{\lambda\sqrt{p}}\bigg).
\end{align*}
By symmetry among indices, it holds that with probability at least $1 - O(p^{-9})$ that
\begin{align}
    \mathcal{\widehat T}_{ijk} - \mathcal{T}_{ijk} &= e_i^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_1 \mathbf{V}_1 \mathbf{V}_1^{\top} e_{(j-1)p_3 + k} + e_j^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_2 \mathbf{V}_2 \mathbf{V}_2^{\top} e_{(k-1)p_1 + i} + e_k^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_3 \mathbf{V}_3 \mathbf{V}_3^{\top} e_{(i-1)p_2 + j} \nonumber\\
    &\quad + O\bigg( \frac{\kappa^2 \sigma^2 \mu_0^4 \log(p) r^2}{\lambda \sqrt{p}} + \frac{\kappa^2 \mu_0^3 r^2 \sigma}{p^{3/2}} \bigg) \nonumber \\
    &\quad + O\bigg( \frac{\sigma \mu_0^3 \sqrt{\log(p)} r^{3/2}}{p^{3/2}} + \frac{\sigma^2 \mu_0^3 r^{3/2} \kappa \log(p)}{\lambda \sqrt{p}} \bigg) \nonumber \\
   
   
 
    &= e_i^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_1 \mathbf{V}_1 \mathbf{V}_1^{\top} e_{(j-1)p_3 + k} + e_j^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_2 \mathbf{V}_2 \mathbf{V}_2^{\top} e_{(k-1)p_1 + i} + e_k^{\top} \mathbf{Z}_3 \mathbf{V}_3 \mathbf{V}_3^{\top} e_{(i-1)p_2 + j} \nonumber\\
    &\quad + O\bigg(\frac{\sigma \kappa^2 \mu_0^3 r^2 \sqrt{ \log(p)}}{p^{3/2}} \bigg)+  O\bigg( \frac{\sigma^2 \mu_0^4 \kappa^3 r^{2} \log(p)}{\lambda \sqrt{p}}\bigg). \label{mainentrywiseexpansion}
\end{align}
This establishes the leading-order expansion.  

Therefore, defining $\xi_{ijk}$ as in \cref{lem:xiijkgaussian}, with probability at least $1 - O(p^{-9})$ it holds that
\begin{align*}
\frac{\mathcal{T}_{ijk} - \mathcal{\widehat T}_{ijk}}{s_{ijk}} &= \frac{\xi_{ijk}}{s_{ijk}} + \frac{C_1}{s_{ijk}} \frac{\sigma \kappa^2 \mu_0^3 r^2 \sqrt{ \log(p)}}{p^{3/2}} + \frac{C_2}{s_{ijk}}   \frac{\sigma^2 \mu_0^4 \kappa^3 r^{2} \log(p)}{\lambda \sqrt{p}} 
\\
&\coloneqq \frac{\xi_{ijk}}{s_{ijk}} + \frac{\mathrm{err}}{s_{ijk}}
,\end{align*}
where $C_1$ and $C_2$ are some universal constants.  Therefore,  for any $t \in \mathbb{R}$, by \cref{lem:xiijkgaussian}, it holds that
\begin{align*}
    \mathbb{P}\Bigg\{ \frac{\mathcal{T}_{ijk} - \mathcal{\widehat T}_{ijk}}{s_{ijk}} \leq t \Bigg\} &\leq \mathbb{P}\Bigg\{\frac{\xi_{ijk}}{s_{ijk}} \leq t + \frac{\mathrm{err}}{s_{ijk}} \Bigg\}  + C_3 p^{-9} \\
    &\leq \Phi\Bigg\{ t + \frac{\mathrm{err}}{s_{ijk}} \Bigg\}+ C_3 p^{-9} + \frac{C_4}{\sqrt{p\log(p)}} + \frac{C_5 \mu_0^2 r}{p} \\
    &\leq \Phi(t) + \frac{\mathrm{err}}{s_{ijk}} + C_3 p^{-9} + \frac{C_4}{\sqrt{p\log(p)}} + \frac{C_5 \mu_0^2 r}{p} \\
    &= \Phi(t) + o(1),
\end{align*}
where the final result holds since
\begin{align*}
    s_{ijk} &\geq \sigma_{\min} \left(\left\|e_{(j-1) p_{3}+k}^{\top} \mathbf{V}_{1}\right\|^{2}+\left\|e_{(k-1) p_{1}+i} \mathbf{V}_{2}\right\|^{2}+\left\|e_{(i-1) p_{2}+j} \mathbf{V}_{3}\right\|^{2}\right)^{1 / 2} \\
    &\gg \sigma_{\min} \max\bigg\{ \frac{\kappa^2 \mu_0^3 r^2 \sqrt{\log(p)}}{p^{3/2}}, \frac{\sigma \mu_0^4 \kappa^3 r^2 \log(p)}{\lambda \sqrt{p}} \bigg\}, 
   
\end{align*}
and the fact that $\sigma/\sigma_{\min} = O(1)$.  By applying the same argument to the other direction, the proof is complete.

The proof is similar to \cref{lem:zentrywiselemma}.  Again, observe that \cref{cor:asymptoticnormality_projection} and the conditions of \cref{thm:asymptoticnormalityentries} implies that with probability at least $1 - O(p^{-9})$,
\begin{align*}
    \max_k \| \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_k {\mathbf{U}}_k^{\top} \|_{2,\infty} &\lesssim \frac{\sigma \mu_0 \sqrt{r\log(p)}}{\lambda}.
\end{align*}
Therefore, we note that on this event,
\begin{align*}
    \bigg| \bigg( \mathcal{T}& \times_1 (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_1{\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top}) \times_2 ( \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top}) \times_3 ({\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top}) \bigg)_{ijk} \bigg| \\
    &= \bigg| e_k^{\top} {\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top} \mathbf{T}_3 \bigg( (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_1{\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top}) \otimes ( \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top}) \bigg) e_{(i-1)p_2 + j} \bigg| \\
    &\leq \| {\mathbf{U}}_3 \|_{2,\infty} \| {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top} \mathbf{T}_3 \| \bigg\| \bigg( (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_1{\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top}) \otimes ( \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top}) \bigg) \bigg\|_{2,\infty} \\
    &\leq \lambda_1 \| {\mathbf{U}}_3 \|_{2,\infty} \| \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_1{\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top} \|_{2,\infty} \| \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top} \|_{2,\infty} \\
    &\lesssim \lambda_1 \mu_0 \sqrt{\frac{r}{p}} \frac{ \sigma^2 \mu_0^2 r\log(p)}{\lambda^2} \\
    &\lesssim \frac{\sigma^2 \mu_0^3 r^{3/2} \kappa \log(p)}{\lambda\sqrt{p}}.
\end{align*}
Similarly, also on this event,
\begin{align*}
    \bigg|\bigg( &\mathcal{T} \times_1 (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_1{\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top}) \times_2 ( \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top}) \times_3 (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_3 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_3^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top}) \bigg)_{ijk} \bigg| \\
    &= \bigg| e_i^{\top} (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_1{\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top}) \mathbf{T}_1\bigg[ \bigg( \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top} \bigg) \otimes \bigg( \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_3 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_3^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top} \bigg) \bigg] e_{(j-1)p_3 + k} \bigg| \\
    &\leq \| \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_1^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_1{\mathbf{U}}_1^{\top} \|_{2,\infty} \| \mathbf{T}_1 \| \| \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_2^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_2 {\mathbf{U}}_2^{\top} \|_{2,\infty} \| \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_3 \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_3^{\top} - {\mathbf{U}}_3 {\mathbf{U}}_3^{\top} \|_{2,\infty} \\
    &\leq \frac{\sigma^3 \mu_0^3 r^{3/2} \kappa\log^{3/2}(p)}{\lambda^2} \\
    &\lesssim \frac{\sigma^2 \mu_0^3 r^{3/2} \kappa \log(p)}{\lambda\sqrt{p}},
\end{align*} 
since $\lambda/\sigma \gtrsim \sqrt{p\log(p)}$.  This completes the proof.

nodes.name: Proof of \cref{lem:xiijkgaussian}
nodes.statement: We first observe that the random variable xi_ijk &coloneqq e_i^top Z_1 V_1 V_1^top e_(j-1) p_3+k+e_j^top Z_2 V_2 V_2^top e_(k-1) p_1+i+e_k^top Z_3 V_3 V_3^top e_(i-1) p_2+j is a linear combination of random variables belonging to Z. Note that Var(xi_ijk) may not equal s^2_ijk. First, we will show that Var(xi_ijk) &= s^2_ijk + o( s^2_ijk). Next, we will calculate the moment bounds needed to apply the Berry-Esseen Theorem, and finally we will put it all together. item Step 1: Variance Calculation: Since xi_ijk is a sum of three separate terms, we will first calculate the contribution of the cross terms to the variance of xi_ijk. \label{lem:Vmatrixcloseness} Instate the conditions of \cref{thm:eigenvectornormality}, and suppose that $$\kappa^2 \mu_0^2 r^{3/2} \sqrt{\log(p)} \lesssim p^{1/4}.$$
Let $\mathbf{\widehat V}_k$ and $\mathbf{\widehat \Lambda}_k$ be as in \cref{al:ci_eigenvector} and \cref{al:ci_entries}.  Let $\mathbf{W}_{\mathbf{V}_k} \coloneqq \mathrm{sgn}(\mathbf{ V}_k^{\top} \mathbf{\widehat V}_k)$.  Then with probability at least $1 - O(p^{-9})$,
\begin{align*}
\max_k \| \sin\Theta(\mathbf{\widehat V}_k,\mathbf{V}_k) \| &\lesssim \frac{\sigma \sqrt{pr} + \kappa^2 \sigma \sqrt{p\log(p)}}{\lambda}; \\
\max_k   \| \mathbf{\widehat V}_k - \mathbf{V}_k \mathbf{W}_{\mathbf{V}_k} \|_{2,\infty} &\lesssim \frac{\kappa^2 \sigma \mu_0^2 r^{3/2} \sqrt{\log(p)}}{\lambda \sqrt{p}}; \\
\max_k  \| \mathbf{W}_{\mathbf{V}_k}^{\top} \mathbf{\Lambda}_k^{-1} - \mathbf{\widehat{\Lambda}}_k^{-1} \mathbf{\widehat W}_k^{\top} \| &\lesssim \frac{1}{\lambda} \bigg( \frac{\sigma \sqrt{pr} + \kappa^2 \sigma \sqrt{p\log(p)}}{\lambda} \bigg).
\end{align*}

Here we suppress the dependence on $t$. \cref{lem:gammacloseness} reveals that
\begin{align*}
   \| \mathbf{\widehat W}_k&\big(\mathbf{\widehat \Gamma}^{(m)}_k \big)^{1/2}\mathbf{\widehat W}_k^{\top} -\big(\mathbf{\Gamma}^{(m)}_k \big)^{1/2} \|  \\
   &\lesssim \frac{\sigma}{\lambda} \bigg( \frac{\sigma r \sqrt{p}\log(p) + \sigma \kappa^2 \sqrt{rp} \log^{3/2}(p)}{\lambda} + \frac{\kappa \mu_0 \sqrt{r} \log(p)}{p} + \frac{\mu_0 r^{3/2} \sqrt{\log(p)}}{p} \bigg) \\
   &= \frac{\sigma}{\lambda} \times o(1)
\end{align*}
with probability at least $1 - O(p^{-6})$.  Snce $\mathbf{\Gamma}_k^{(m)}$ has smallest eigenvalue at most $c\frac{\sigma^2}{\lambda}$ (see the proof of \cref{lem:gammacloseness}), by Weyl's inequality it therefore holds that
\begin{align}
    \lambda_{\min} \bigg( \big(\mathbf{\widehat \Gamma}^{(m)}_k \big)^{1/2}\bigg) \gtrsim \frac{\sigma_{\min}}{\lambda}. \label{lowerbdongamma}
\end{align}
Hence, with probability at least $1 - O(p^{-6})$ it holds that
\begin{align*}
    \| e_m^{\top} \bigg( &\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k \mathbf{W}_k^{\top}- {\mathbf{U}}_k   \bigg) \big( (\mathbf{\Gamma}^{(m)}_k)^{-1/2} - (\mathbf{W}_k \mathbf{\widehat \Gamma}^{(m)}_k \mathbf{W}_k^{\top} )^{-1/2} \big) \| \\
    &\leq \| e_m^{\top} \big(  \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k \mathbf{W}_k^{\top}- {\mathbf{U}}_k   \big) \| \| (\mathbf{\Gamma}^{(m)}_k)^{-1/2} - (\mathbf{W}_k \mathbf{\widehat \Gamma}^{(m)}_k \mathbf{W}_k^{\top} )^{-1/2} \| \\
    &\leq \| e_m^{\top} \big( \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k- {\mathbf{U}}_k  \mathbf{W}_k \big) \| \| (\mathbf{\Gamma}^{(m)}_k)^{-1/2} - (\mathbf{W}_k \mathbf{\widehat \Gamma}^{(m)}_k \mathbf{W}_k^{\top} )^{-1/2} \| \\
    &\leq \| \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k - {\mathbf{U}}_k \mathbf{W}_k \|_{2,\infty} \| (\mathbf{\Gamma}^{(m)}_k)^{-1/2} \bigg( (\mathbf{\Gamma}^{(m)}_k)^{1/2} - \mathbf{W}_k(\mathbf{\widehat \Gamma}^{(m)}_k)^{1/2}\mathbf{W}_k^{\top}  \bigg) ( \mathbf{W}_k \mathbf{\widehat \Gamma}^{(m)}_k\mathbf{W}_k^{\top} )^{-1/2} \| \\
    &\lesssim \frac{\kappa \sigma\mu_0 \sqrt{r\log(p)}}{\lambda} \frac{1}{\lambda_{\min}^{1/2}(\mathbf{\Gamma}^{(m)}_k)} \frac{1}{\lambda_{\min}^{1/2}(\mathbf{\widehat \Gamma}^{(m)}_k)} \| (\mathbf{\Gamma}^{(m)}_k)^{1/2} - \mathbf{W}_k(\mathbf{\widehat \Gamma}^{(m)}_k)^{1/2}\mathbf{W}_k^{\top} \| \\
    &\lesssim \frac{\kappa \sigma \mu_0 \sqrt{r\log(p)}}{\lambda} \frac{\lambda^2}{\sigma_{\min}^2} \| (\mathbf{\Gamma}^{(m)}_k)^{1/2} - \mathbf{W}_k(\mathbf{\widehat \Gamma}^{(m)}_k)^{1/2}\mathbf{W}_k^{\top} \| \\
    &\lesssim \kappa \mu_0 \sqrt{r\log(p)} \bigg( \frac{\sigma r \sqrt{p}\log(p) + \sigma \kappa^2 \sqrt{rp} \log^{3/2}(p)}{\lambda} + \frac{\kappa \mu_0 \sqrt{r} \log(p)}{p} + \frac{\mu_0 r^{3/2} \sqrt{\log(p)}}{p} \bigg) \\
    &\asymp \frac{ \sigma \kappa \mu_0 r^{3/2} \sqrt{p} \log^{3/2}(p) + \sigma \kappa^3 r \mu_0 \sqrt{p} \log^2(p)}{\lambda} + \frac{\kappa^2 \mu_0^2 r \log^{3/2}(p)}{p} + \frac{\kappa \mu_0^2 r^2 \log(p)}{p}\\
    &\coloneqq \varepsilon,
\end{align*}
where in the fourth line we have implicitly used \cref{thm:twoinfty}.  For a convex set $A$, we denote $A^{\varepsilon}$ as the $\varepsilon$-enlargement via
\begin{align*}
    A^{\varepsilon} &\coloneqq \{ x: d(x,A) \leq \varepsilon \}.
\end{align*}
By Theorem 1.2 of \cite{raicv_multivariate_2019}, if $Z$ is an isotropic $\mathbb{R}^{r_k}$ dimensional random vector, it holds that
\begin{align*}
    \mathbb{P}\bigg( Z \in A^{\varepsilon} \setminus A \bigg) &\lesssim r^{1/4} \varepsilon.
\end{align*}
The proof is now straightforward.  Define $A_{\alpha}$ as the confidence region such that
\begin{align*}
    \mathbb{P}( Z \in A_{\alpha} ) = 1 - \alpha,
\end{align*}
where $Z \sim N(0, I_{r_k})$.  Then by \cref{thm:eigenvectornormality2}, 
\begin{align*}
    \bigg| \mathbb{P}\bigg\{ e_m^{\top}& {\mathbf{U}}_k \mathbf{\widehat W}_k \in \mathrm{C.I.}_{\alpha} (\mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k) \bigg\}  - (1-\alpha) \bigg| \\
    &= \bigg| \mathbb{P}\bigg\{ e_m^{\top} \bigg(  {\mathbf{U}}_k \mathbf{\widehat W}_k - \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k \bigg) \in \big(\mathbf{\widehat \Gamma}^{(m)}_k\big)^{1/2} A_{\alpha} \bigg\} - (1 - \alpha) \bigg| \\
    &=\bigg| \mathbb{P}\bigg\{ e_m^{\top} \bigg( {\mathbf{U}}_k - \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k \mathbf{\widehat W}_k^{\top} \bigg) \in  \mathbf{\widehat W}_k \big(\mathbf{\widehat \Gamma}^{(m)}_k\big)^{1/2} \mathbf{\widehat W}_k^{\top} A_{\alpha} \bigg\} - (1-\alpha) \bigg| \\
    &\leq \bigg| \mathbb{P}\Bigg\{ \bigg\{ e_m^{\top} \bigg( {\mathbf{U}}_k - \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k \mathbf{\widehat W}_k^{\top} \bigg) \in \big( \mathbf{\Gamma}^{(m)}_k\big)^{1/2} A_{\alpha}\bigg\} \\
    &\quad \bigcap \bigg\{ \bigg\| e_m^{\top} \bigg( {\mathbf{U}}_k - \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k \mathbf{\widehat W}_k^{\top} \bigg) \bigg( \big( \mathbf{\Gamma}^{(m)}_k \big)^{-1/2} - \mathbf{W}_k \big(\mathbf{\widehat \Gamma}^{(m)}_k \big)^{-1/2} \mathbf{W}_k^{\top} \bigg) \bigg\| \leq \varepsilon \bigg\} \Bigg\} \\
    &\qquad - (1- \alpha) \bigg| \\
    &\qquad + \mathbb{P}\bigg\{ \bigg\| e_m^{\top} \bigg( {\mathbf{U}}_k - \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k \mathbf{\widehat W}_k^{\top} \bigg) \bigg( \big( \mathbf{\Gamma}^{(m)}_k \big)^{-1/2} - \mathbf{W}_k \big(\mathbf{\widehat \Gamma}^{(m)}_k \big)^{-1/2} \mathbf{W}_k^{\top} \bigg) \bigg\| >  \varepsilon \bigg\} \\
    &\leq \bigg| \mathbb{P}\bigg\{ e_m^{\top} \bigg( {\mathbf{U}}_k - \mathbf{\widehat{U}}_k \mathbf{\widehat W}_k^{\top} \bigg) \in \big(\mathbf{\Gamma}^{(m)}_k \big)^{1/2} A_{\alpha}^{\varepsilon} - (1- \alpha) \bigg| \\
    &\quad + p^{-6} \\
    &\lesssim \bigg| \mathbb{P}\bigg\{ Z \in A_{\alpha}^{\varepsilon} \bigg\} - (1 - \alpha) \bigg| \\
    &\quad + \frac{\mu_0 r^2}{p} + \frac{\sigma \kappa^3 \mu_0^2 \log(p) r^{3/2} \sqrt{p}}{\lambda} + \frac{\mu_0 r^{3/2} \kappa}{\sqrt{p}} + p^{-6} \\
    &\lesssim \bigg| \mathbb{P}\bigg( Z \in A_{\alpha} \bigg) - (1 - \alpha) \bigg| \\
    &\quad + \mathbb{P}\bigg\{ Z \in A_{\alpha}^{\varepsilon} \setminus A \bigg\} \\
    &\quad +  \frac{\mu_0 r^2}{p} + \frac{\sigma \kappa^3 \mu_0^2 \log(p) r^{3/2} \sqrt{p}}{\lambda} + \frac{\mu_0 r^{3/2} \kappa}{\sqrt{p}} + p^{-6}\\
    &\lesssim r^{1/4} \varepsilon + + \frac{\mu_0 r^2}{p} + \frac{\sigma \kappa^3 \mu_0^2 \log(p) r^{3/2} \sqrt{p}}{\lambda} + \frac{\mu_0 r^{3/2} \kappa}{\sqrt{p}} + p^{-6} \\
    &\lesssim r^{1/2} \varepsilon + + \frac{\mu_0 r^2}{p} + \frac{\sigma \kappa^3 \mu_0^2 \log(p) r^{3/2} \sqrt{p}}{\lambda} + \frac{\mu_0 r^{3/2} \kappa}{\sqrt{p}} + p^{-6} \\
    &\lesssim r^{1/2} \bigg( \frac{ \sigma \kappa \mu_0 r^{3/2} \sqrt{p} \log^{3/2}(p) + \sigma \kappa^3 r \mu_0 \sqrt{p} \log^2(p)}{\lambda} + \frac{\kappa^2 \mu_0^2 r \log^{3/2}(p)}{p} + \frac{\kappa \mu_0^2 r^2 \log(p)}{p} \bigg) \\
    &\quad +\frac{\mu_0 r^2}{p} + \frac{\sigma \kappa^3 \mu_0^2 \log(p) r^{3/2} \sqrt{p}}{\lambda} + \frac{\mu_0 r^{3/2} \kappa}{\sqrt{p}} + p^{-6} \\
    &= o(1),
\end{align*}
where the term is $o(1)$ as long as
\begin{align*}
    \lambda/\sigma \gg \kappa^3 \mu_0^2 \log^2(p) r^2 \sqrt{p},
\end{align*}
which is true by assumption, and 
\begin{align*}
    \kappa^2 \mu_0^2 r^{3/2} \log^{3/2}(p) + \kappa \mu_0^2 r^{5/2} \log(p) \ll p
\end{align*}
which holds as long as $\kappa^2 \mu_0^2 r^{3/2} \sqrt{\log(p)} \lesssim p^{1/4}$, which is also by assumption. This completes the proof.
