nodes.statement: The proof is similar to the proof of crefthm:civalidity. First, by the proof of crefthm:asymptoticnormalityentries, by applying the main expansion to each entry separately, we have that with probability at least 1 - O(|J|p^-9), it holds that T_J &= xi_J + Obigg( |J|fracsigma kappa^2 mu_0^3 r^3/2 sqrtlog(p)p^3/2 + |J| fracsigma^2 mu_0^4 kappa^3 r^2 log(p)lambda sqrtp bigg), where we set xi_J as the random variable with entries xi_ijk from creflem:xiijkgaussian. We will show that xi_J is asymptotically Gaussian with covariance S_J, and we will demonstrate that widehat S_J approximates S_J, which will yield the result. item Step 1: Limiting Covariance Structure and First-Order Approximation: Recall we define s^2_min via s^2_min coloneqq lambda_min(S_J), If it holds that s_min &gg |J| sigmamaxbigg\ frac kappa^2 mu_0^3 r^3/2 sqrtlog(p)p^3/2, fracsigma mu_0^4 kappa^3 r^2 log(p)lambda sqrtpbigg\, then S_J^-1/2 Vec(T_J) &= S_J^-1/2 xi_J + o(1). with probability at least 1 - O(|J|p^-9). It now remains to show that Cov(xi_J) approx S_J. By the proof of creflem:xiijkgaussian, it holds that Var(xi_ijk) &= s^2_ijk bigg( 1 + Obig( fracmu_0^2 rp big) bigg). Therefore, it suffices to consider the covariance terms. Observe that &Covbigg( xi_ijk xi_i'j'k'bigg) \\&= Ebigg( e_i^top Z_1 V_1 V_1^top e_(j-1) p_3+k+e_j^top Z_2 V_2 V_2^top e_(k-1) p_1+i+e_k^top Z_3 V_3 V_3^top e_(i-1) p_2+j bigg)\\ &times bigg( e_i'^top Z_1 V_1 V_1^top e_(j'-1) p_3+k'+e_j'^top Z_2 V_2 V_2^top e_(k'-1) p_1+i'+e_k'^top Z_3 V_3 V_3^top e_(i'-1) p_2+j' bigg). By a similar argument to Step 1 of the proof of creflem:xiijkgaussian, it holds that the cross term satisfies E&bigg( e_i^top Z_1 V_1 V_1^top e_(j-1)p_3 + kbigg) bigg( e_j'^top Z_2 V_2 V_2^top e_(k'-1)p_1 + i' bigg) \\ &= Obigg( sigma^2 mu_0^2 fracrp bigg( \| e_(j-1)p_3 + k V_1 \|^2 + \| e_(k'-1)p_1 + i' V_2 \|^2 bigg) bigg) \\ &= Obigg( sigma^2 mu_0^4 fracr^2p^2 bigg). The other cross terms can be handled similarly. Hence, the only remaining terms are those such that i = i', j = j', or k = k'. If i= i', we have Ebigg( &e_i^top Z_1 V_1^top e_(j-1)p_3 + k bigg)bigg( e_i^top Z_1 V_1^top e_(j'-1)p_3 + k' bigg) I_\i=i'\\\ &= e_(j-1)p_2 + k^top V_1 V_1^top big( Sigma^(i) big) V_1 V_1^top e_(j'-1)p_3 + k', with similar values if j = j' or k = k'; in particular, these are the entries of S_J by definition. Hence Cov(xi_J) &= S_J + Obigg( frac|J|^2mu_0^2 rp s_min^2 bigg), provided that s_min^2 gg sigma^2 mu_0^2 r/p. item Step 2: Gaussian Approximation: We now study the Gaussian approximation of the vector S_J^-1/2 Vec(T_J - widehat T_J). We will apply Corollary 2.2 of . Define, for some sufficiently large constant C, Delta = Delta^(i) &= C left(|J| fracsigma kappa^2 mu_0^3 r^3 / 2 sqrtlog (p)p^3 / 2+|J| fracsigma^2 mu_0^4 kappa^3 r^2 log (p)lambda sqrtpright). Note that Cov(xi_J) is invertible with smallest eigenvalue at least s^2_min(1- o(1)) since S_J is invertible provided that |J|^2 ll p /(mu_0^2 r). Consequently, we have that lambda_minbig( Cov^1/2(xi_J)big) &gtrsim s_min gg Delta as long as s_min &gg |J| max bigg\ fracsigma kappa^2 mu_0^3 r^3 / 2 sqrtlog (p)p^3 / 2, fracsigma^2 mu_0^4 kappa^3 r^2 log (p)lambda sqrtpbigg\. Hence, it holds that Cov(xi_J)^-1/2 Vec(T_J) &= Cov(xi_J)^-1/2 xi_J + fracDeltas_min with probability at least 1 - O(|J|p^-9). Let this event be denoted A. By Corollary 2.2 of , it holds that sup_A in A bigg| &Pbigg\ Cov^-1/2 Vec(T_J - widehat T_J) in A bigg\ - Pbigg\ Z in A bigg\ bigg| \\ &lesssim |J|^1/2gamma + fracDeltas_min E \| Cov^-1/2xi_J \|+ |J|p^-9, where gamma is the sum of the third moments of the independent random variables in xi_J (see step 2 of the proof of creflem:xiijkgaussian for the explicit definition in terms of the indices of xi_J). A straightforward modification of the proof of creflem:xiijkgaussian shows that gamma &lesssim frac|J|sqrtplog(p) as long as s_min gg Delta, which is true by assumption. In addition, by subgaussianity, it holds that E \| Cov^-1/2( xi_J) xi_J \| &lesssim | J |^1/2. Consequently, we have that sup_A in A &bigg| Pbigg\ Cov(xi_J)^-1/2 Vec(T_J - widehat T_J) in A bigg\ - Pbigg\ Z in A bigg\ bigg| \\ &lesssim frac|J|^3/2sqrtplog(p) + |J|p^-9 + |J|^1/2 Delta \\ &lesssim frac|J|^3/2sqrtp log(p) + frac |J|^3/2s_min left( fracsigma kappa^2 mu_0^3 r^3 / 2 sqrtlog (p)p^3 / 2+ fracsigma^2 mu_0^4 kappa^3 r^2 log (p)lambda sqrtpright), which holds as long as s_min gg |J| fracsigma kappa^2 mu_0^3 r^3 / 2 sqrtlog (p)p^3 / 2+|J| fracsigma^2 mu_0^4 kappa^3 r^2 log (p)lambda sqrtp. Therefore, for any A in A, bigg| &Pbigg\ S_J^-1/2 Vec(T_J - widehat T_J) in A bigg\ - P bigg\ Z in A bigg\ bigg| \\ &leq bigg| Pbigg\ Cov(xi_J)^-1/2(Vec(T_J - widehat T_J) in Cov(xi_J)^-1/2 S_J^1/2 A bigg\ - Pbigg\ Z' in Cov(xi_J)^-1/2 S_J^1/2 A bigg\ bigg| \\ & + bigg| Pbigg\ Z' in Cov(xi_J)^-1/2 S_J^1/2 A bigg\ - Pbigg\ Z in A bigg\ bigg| \\ &lesssim frac|J|^3/2sqrtplog(p) + frac |J|^3/2s_minbigg( fracsigma kappa^2 mu_0^3 r^3/2 sqrtlog(p)p^3/2 + fracsigma^2 mu_0^4 kappa^3 r^2 log(p)lambda sqrtp bigg) \\ & + bigg| Pbigg\ Z' in Cov(xi_J)^-1/2 S_J^1/2 A bigg\ - Pbigg\ Z in A bigg\ bigg| where Z' is an independent |J|-dimensional standard Gaussian random variable. To bound the remaining term, by Theorem 1.3 of , it holds that sup_A in A bigg| Pbigg\ S_J^-1/2 Cov(xi_J)^1/2Z in A bigg\ - Pbigg\ Z' in A bigg\ bigg| &leq d_TV ( S_J^-1/2 Cov(xi_J)^1/2Z, Z' ) \\ &lesssim \| I - S_J^-1 Cov(xi_J) \| \\ &lesssim |J|^2 mu_0^2 fracrp, where the final inequality holds by . Putting it all together, it holds that sup_A in A bigg| &Pbigg\ S_J^-1/2 Vec(T_J - widehat T_J) in A bigg\ - Pbigg\ Z in A bigg\ bigg| nonumber \\&lesssim frac|J|^3/2sqrtplog(p) + frac|J|^2mu_0^2 rp +frac |J|^3/2s_minbigg( fracsigma kappa^2 mu_0^3 r^3/2 sqrtlog(p)p^3/2 + fracsigma^2 mu_0^4 kappa^3 r^2 log(p)lambda sqrtp bigg). We note that this bound is only non-vacuous if these terms are smaller than one, which requires that s_min &gg |J|^3/2 maxbigg\ fracsigma kappa^2 mu_0^3 r^3/2 sqrtlog(p)p^3/2 , fracsigma^2 mu_0^4 kappa^3 r^2 log(p)lambda sqrtp bigg\, which is the stronger than the requirements ,, and by factors of |J|. item Step 3: Covariance Estimation: We now consider the plug-in estimation of the covariance S_J. The proof of crefthm:civalidity shows that with probability at least 1 - O(p^-6) |(s^(i))^2 - (widehat s^(i))^2 | &lesssim sigma^2 mu_0 fracsqrtr log(p)p \| e_(j-1)p_3 + k^top V_1 \|^2 + fracsigma^2 kappa mu_0^2 r^3/2 log(p)p^3 \\ & + fracsigma^3 mu_0^5 r^3 kappa^2 log^3/2(p)lambda p^3/2, with similar bounds for s^(j) and s^(k), where the notation is defined in the proof of crefthm:civalidity (see crefsec:civalidityproofs). A straightfoward modification of the same proof for the cross-terms reveals that with probability at least 1 - O(|J|^2 p^-6) \| &S_J - widehat S_J \| \\ &leq |J|^2 \| S_J - widehat S_J \|_max \\ &lesssim |J|^2 sigma^2 mu_0^3 frac r^3/2 sqrtlog(p)p^3 + |J|^2bigg( fracsigma^2 kappa mu_0^2 r^3/2 log(p)p^3 + fracsigma^3 mu_0^5 r^3 kappa^2 log^3/2(p)lambda p^3/2 bigg) \\ &ll s^2_min, where the penultimate inequality holds as long as s_min^2 &gg |J|^2 maxbigg\ fracsigma^2 mu_0^3 r^3/2 sqrtlog(p)p^3, fracsigma^2 kappa mu_0^2 r^3/2 log(p)p^3, fracsigma^3 mu_0^5 r^3 kappa^2 log^3/2(p)lambda p^3/2 bigg\. Denote M &coloneqq |J|^2 sigma^2 mu_0^3 frac r^3/2 sqrtlog(p)p^3 + |J|^2bigg( fracsigma^2 kappa mu_0^2 r^3/2 log(p)p^3 + fracsigma^3 mu_0^5 r^3 kappa^2 log^3/2(p)lambda p^3/2 bigg), so that it holds that \| S_J - widehat S_J \| lesssim M with probability at least 1 - O(|J|^2 p^-6). By Theorem 6.2 of , it holds that \| widehat S_J^1/2 - S_J^1/2 \| &leq frac1 lambda_min^1/2(widehat S_J) + lambda_min^1/2(S_J) \| widehat S_J - S_J \| \\ &lesssim frac1s_min M \\ &ll s_min provided M ll s^2_min. Therefore, by Weyl's inequality, widehat S_J is invertible and \| bigg( S_J^-1/2 - widehat S_J^-1/2 bigg) (widehat T_J - T_J ) \| &leq |J | \| widehat T - T \|_max \| S_J^-1/2 - widehat S_J^-1/2 \| \\ &leq |J| \| S_J^-1/2 ( widehat S_J^1/2 - S_J^1/2) widehat S_J^-1/2 \| \| widehat T - T \|_max \\ &lesssim |J| \| widehat T - T \|_max frac1s_min^2 \| widehat S_J^1/2 - S_J^1/2 \| \\ &lesssim |J| \| widehat T - T \|_max frac1s_min^3 M \\ &lesssim frac|J| M s_min^3 bigg( fracsigma kappa mu_0 sqrtr log (p)p+fracsigma^2 mu_0^4 kappa^3 r^3 log (p)lambda sqrtp bigg) \\ &=: varepsilon, where we note that the final inequality holds with probability at least 1 - O(p^-6) by crefcor:maxnormbound. item Step 4: Completing the Proof: Just as in the proof of crefthm:civalidity2, for a convex set A denote A^varepsilon as the varepsilon-enlargment via A^varepsilon &coloneqq \x : d(x,A) leq varepsilon \. By Theorem 1.2 of , if A is an isotropic R^|J|-dimensional random gaussian vector, it holds that Pbigg( Z in A^varepsilonsetminus Abigg) &lesssim |J|^1/4 varepsilon lesssim |J|^1/2 varepsilon. We are now prepared to complete the proof. Let A_alpha denote the confidence region such that P(Z in A_alpha) = 1 - alpha, where Z sim N(0, I_|J|). Then bigg|P&bigg\ Vec(T_J) in C.I._alpha(widehat T_J) bigg\ - (1 - alpha) bigg| \\ &= bigg| Pbigg\ widehat S_J^-1/2bigg( Vecbig( widehat T_J - T_J big) bigg) in A_alpha bigg\ - (1 - alpha) bigg| \\ &leq bigg| Pbigg\ S_J^-1/2 bigg( Vecbig( widehat T_J - T_J big) bigg) in A_alpha^varepsilon bigg\ cap bigg\bigg|big( S_J^-1/2 - widehat S_J^-1/2big) bigg( Vecbig( widehat T_J - T_J big) bigg)bigg| leq varepsilon bigg\ \\ & - (1 - alpha) bigg| \\ & + Pbigg\ bigg|big( S_J^-1/2 - widehat S_J^-1/2big) bigg( Vecbig( widehat T_J - T_J big) bigg) big| > varepsilon bigg\ \\ &leq bigg| Pbigg\ S_J^-1/2 bigg( Vecbig( widehat T_J - T_J big) bigg) in A_alpha^varepsilon bigg\ - (1- alpha) bigg|+ O(|J|^2p^-6) \\ &leq bigg| Pbigg\ S_J^-1/2 bigg( Vecbig( widehat T_J - T_J big) bigg) in A_alpha^varepsilon bigg\ - Pbigg\ Z in A_alpha^varepsilon bigg\ bigg| + bigg| Pbigg\ Z in A_alpha^varepsilon bigg\ - (1 - alpha) bigg| \\ & + O(|J|^2p^-6) \\ &lesssim frac|J|^3/2sqrtplog(p) + frac|J|^2mu_0^2 rp +frac |J|^3/2s_minbigg( fracsigma kappa^2 mu_0^3 r^3/2 sqrtlog(p)p^3/2 + fracsigma^2 mu_0^4 kappa^3 r^2 log(p)lambda sqrtp bigg) \\ & + bigg| Pbigg\ Z in A_alpha^varepsilon bigg\ - Pbigg\ Z in A_alpha bigg\ bigg| + O(|J|^2p^-6) \\ &lesssim frac|J|^3/2sqrtplog(p) + frac|J|^2mu_0^2 rp +frac |J|^3/2s_minbigg( fracsigma kappa^2 mu_0^3 r^3/2 sqrtlog(p)p^3/2 + fracsigma^2 mu_0^4 kappa^3 r^2 log(p)lambda sqrtp bigg) \\ & + P( Z in A^varepsilon_alpha setminus A_alpha) + O(|J|^2p^-6) \\ &lesssim frac|J|^3/2sqrtplog(p) + frac|J|^2mu_0^2 rp +frac |J|^3/2s_minbigg( fracsigma kappa^2 mu_0^3 r^3/2 sqrtlog(p)p^3/2 + fracsigma^2 mu_0^4 kappa^3 r^2 log(p)lambda sqrtp bigg) \\ & + |J|^1/2 varepsilon + O(|J|^2p^-6), where we have used . In order to complete the proof we need that this final bound is of order o(1). For the first two terms to be o(1), we see that J needs to satisfy |J| &ll minbigg\ p^1/6, fracp^1/2mu_0 r^1/2 bigg\; This is guaranteed if |J| = o(p^1/6), since we assume that mu_0^2 r lesssim sqrtp, so that fracp^1/2mu_0 r^1/2 gtrsim p^1/4. This also is sufficient for the probability terms to be o(1). We now translate the conditions on s_min. First we collect all our requirements from the previous steps. From steps 1 and 2, requires that s_min &gg |J|^3/2 sigma maxbigg\ frackappa^2 mu_0^3 r^3/2 sqrtlog(p)p^3/2, fracsigma mu_0^4 kappa^3 r^2 log(p)lambda sqrtp bigg\. In addition, from , we require s_min^2 &gg |J|^2 maxbigg\ fracsigma^2 mu_0^3 r^3/2 sqrtlog(p)p^3, fracsigma^2 kappa mu_0^2 r^3/2 log(p)p^3, fracsigma^3 mu_0^5 r^3 kappa^2 log^3/2(p)lambda p^3/2 bigg\. Recalling the definition of M in , this condition is equivalent to the condition s_min^3 &gg sigma |J|^7/2 maxbigg\ frac kappa mu_0 sqrtrlog(p)p, fracsigma mu_0^4 kappa^3 r^3 log(p)lambda sqrtp bigg\ \\ &times bigg( mu_0 fracsqrtr log(p)p s_min^2 + sigma^2 mu_0^3 frac r^3/2 sqrtlog(p)p^3 nonumber+ fracsigma^2 kappa mu_0^2 r^3/2 log(p)p^3 + fracsigma^3 mu_0^5 r^3 kappa^2 log^3/2(p)lambda p^3/2 bigg). When |J| = o(p^1/6) and kappa^2 mu_0^2 r^3/2 sqrtlog(p) lesssim p^1/4 this condition is satisfied when s_min^3 &gg sigma |J|^7/2 maxbigg\ frackappa mu_0 sqrtrlog(p)p, fracsigma mu_0^4 kappa^3 r^2 log(p)lambda sqrtp bigg\ \\ & times maxbigg\ fracsigma^2 mu_0^3 r^3/2 sqrtlog(p)p^3, fracsigma^2 kappa mu_0^2 r^3/2log(p)p^3, fracsigma^3 mu_0^5 kappa^2 log^3/2(p)lambda p^3/2 bigg\ \\ &asymp sigma^3 |J|^7/2 maxbigg\ frackappa mu_0^4 r^2 log(p)p^4, frackappa^2 mu_0^3 r^2 log^3/2(p)p^4, frackappa^3 mu_0^6 sqrtr log^2(p) (lambda/sigma) p^5/2,\\ & frackappa^3 mu_0^7 r^7/2 log^3/2(p) (lambda/sigma) p^7/2, frackappa^4 mu_0^6 r^7/2 log^2(p)(lambda/sigma) p^7/2, frackappa^5 mu_0^9 r^2 log^5/2(p)(lambda/sigma)^2 p^5/2 bigg\ Putting it together and putting terms on the same scale, we see that we have the three conditions s_min/sigma &gg |J|^3/2maxbigg\ frackappa^2 mu_0^3 r^3/2 sqrtlog(p)p^3/2, fracsigma mu_0^4 kappa^3 r^2 log(p)lambda sqrtp bigg\; \\ s_min/sigma &gg |J| maxbigg\ frac mu_0^3/2 r^3/4 log^1/4(p)p^3/2, frac kappa^1/2 mu_0 r^3/4 sqrtlog(p)p^3/2, frac mu_0^5/2 r^3/2 kappa log^3/4(p)(lambda/sigma)^1/2 p^3/4 bigg\; \\ s_min/sigma &gg |J|^1/6 maxbigg\ frackappa^1/3mu_0^4/3 r^2/3 log^1/3(p)p^4/3, frackappa^2/3 mu_0 r^2/3 log^1/2(p)p^4/3, frackappa mu_0^2 r^1/6 log^2/3(p)(lambda/sigma)^1/3 p^5/6, \\ & frackappa mu_0^7/3 r^7/6 log^1/2(p)(lambda/sigma)^1/3 p^7/6, frackappa^4/3 mu_0^2 r^7/6 log^2/3(p)(lambda/sigma)^1/3p^7/6, frackappa^5/3mu_0^3 r^2/3 log^5/6(p)(lambda/sigma)^2/3 p^5/6 bigg\. Removing redundant conditions shows that we require s_min/sigma &gg maxbigg\ |J|^3/2 frackappa^2 mu_0^3 r^3/2 sqrtlog(p)p^3/2, |J|^3/2 frac mu_0^4 kappa^3 r^2 log(p)(lambda/sigma) sqrtp, |J| frac mu_0^5/2 r^3/2 kappa log^3/4(p)(lambda/sigma)^1/2 p^3/4, \\ & |J|^1/6 frackappa mu_0^3/2 r^3/2 sqrtlog(p)p^4/3, |J|^1/6 frackappa^5/3mu_0^3 r^7/6 log^5/6(p)(lambda/sigma)^1/3 p^5/6bigg\. which holds under the conditions of crefthm:simultaneousinference.

nodes.name: Proof of \cref{thm:entrytesting}
nodes.statement: Similar to the previous proof, by the proof of crefthm:asymptoticnormalityentries, by it holds that widehat T_ijk - T_ijk = xi_ijk + Obigg( fracsigma kappa^2 mu_0^3 r^3/2 sqrtlog(p)p^3/2 + fracsigma^2 mu_0^4 kappa^3 r^2 log(p)lambda sqrtp bigg) with probability at least 1 - O(p^-9), where xi_ijk is defined as in creflem:xiijkgaussian. A similar expansion holds for widehat T_i'j'k' - T_i'j'k', which demonstrates that widehat T_ijk - widehat T_i'j'k' - (T_ijk - widehat T_i'j'k') &= xi_ijk - xi_i'j'k' + Obigg( fracsigma kappa^2 mu_0^3 r^3/2 sqrtlog(p)p^3/2 + fracsigma^2 mu_0^4 kappa^3 r^2 log(p)lambda sqrtp bigg). Our proof now proceeds in a similar manner to crefthm:simultaneousinference. item Step 1: Limiting Variance Structure: We first calculate the variance of xi_ijk. However, through precisely the same analysis as in step 1 of crefthm:simultaneousinference, we have that Covbigg( xi_ijk xi_i'j'k' bigg) &= I_\i= i'\ e_(j-1)p_3 + k^top widehat V_1 widehat V_1^top widehat Sigma^(i) widehat V_1 widehat V_1^top e_(j'-1)p_3 + k' \\ & + I_\j= j'\ e_(k-1)p_1 + i^top widehat V_2 widehat V_2^topwidehat Sigma^(j) widehat V_2 widehat V_2^top e_(k'-1)p_3 + i' \\ & + I_\k= k'\ e_(i-1)p_2 + j^top widehat V_3 widehat V_3^top widehat Sigma^(k) widehat V_3 widehat V_3^top e_(i'-1)p_2 +j' \\ & + Obigg( mu_0^2 fracrp bigg[ s^2_ijk + s^2_i'j'k'bigg] bigg). Therefore, Var( xi_ijk - xi_i'j'k') &= s^2_\ijk\\i'j'k'\ bigg(1 + Obigg( mu_0^2 fracrp bigg) bigg). item Step 2: Gaussian Approximation and Variance Approximation: Define, for some sufficiently large constant C, Delta = Delta^(i) = C bigg( fracsigma kappa^2 mu_0^3 r^3/2 sqrtlog(p)p^3/2 + fracsigma^2 mu_0^4 kappa^3 r^2 log(p)lambda sqrtp bigg). Observe that we have the expansion fracwidehat T_ijk - widehat T_i'j'k' - ( T_ijk - T_i'j'k')s_\ijk\\i'j'k'\ &= fracxi_ijk - xi_i'j'k's_\ijk\\i'j'k'\ + fracDeltas_\ijk\\i'j'k'\, which holds with probability at least 1 - O(p^-9). By modifying the proof of creflem:xiijkgaussian, it is straightforward to demonstrate that sup_tin R bigg| Pbigg\ fracxi_ijk - xi_i'j'k's_\ijk\\i'j'k'\ bigg\ - Phi(t) bigg| &leq fracC_1sqrtplog(p) + fracC_2 mu_0^2 rp \\ &coloneqq eta. Hence it holds that Pbigg\ frac widehat T_ijk - widehat T_i'j'k' - (T_ijk - widehat T_i'j'k')s_\ijk\\i'j'k'\ leq t bigg\ &leq Pbigg\ fracxi_ijk - xi_i'j'k's_\ijk\\i'j'k'\ leq t + fracDeltas_\ijk\\i'j'k'\ bigg\ + C_3 p^-9 \\ &leq Phibigg\ t + fracDeltas_\ijk\\i'j'k'\ bigg\ + C_3 p^-9 + eta \\ &leq Phi(t) + fracDeltas_\ijk\\i'j'k'\+ C_3 p^-9 + eta \\ &= Phi(t) + o(1), where the final bounds holds as long as s_\ijk\\i'j'k'\ gg Delta, which we justify at the end of the proof. In addition, it is straightforward to modify the proof of crefthm:civalidity to demonstrate that as long as s^2_\ijk\\i'j'k'\ &gg maxbigg\ fracsigma^2 kappa mu_0^2 r^3/2 log(p)p^3, fracsigma^3 mu_0^5 r^3 kappa^2 log^3/2(p)lambda p^3/2 bigg\ addtocounterequation1tagtheequation it holds that widehat s_\ijk\\i'j'k'\ = s_\ijk\\i'j'k'\(1 +o(1)) with probability at least 1 - O(p^-6). We will check this condition at the end of the proof. Denote the region R_alpha &coloneqq bigg(frac widehat T_ijk - widehat T_i'j'k'widehat s_\ijk\\i'j'k'\ - z_alpha/2 , frac widehat T_ijk - widehat T_i'j'k'widehat s_\ijk\\i'j'k'\ + z_alpha/2bigg). Consequently, by similar manipulations to the end of the proof of crefthm:civalidity, bigg| frac (T_ijk - T_i'j'k')s_\ijk\\i'j'k'\ in R_alpha bigg\ - (1-alpha) bigg| &= o(1). This completes the proof, provided we can justify all of the conditions on s_\ijk\\i'j'k'\. item Step 3: Checking Conditions: Observe that requires that s^2_\ijk\\i'j'k'\ &gg maxbigg\ fracsigma^2 kappa mu_0^2 r^3/2 log(p)p^3, fracsigma^3 mu_0^5 r^3 kappa^2 log^3/2(p)lambda p^3/2 bigg\. In addition, we require that s_\ijk\\i'j'k'\gg Delta. It is sufficient to require that s^2_\ijk\\i'j'k'\ &gg maxbigg\ fracsigma^2 kappa^4 mu_0^6 r^3 log(p)p^3, fracsigma^4 mu_0^8 kappa^6 r^4 log^2(p)lambda^2 p bigg\. Observe that s^2_\ijk\\i'j'k'\ satisfies &s^2_\ijk\\i'j'k'\ \\ &gtrsim sigma^2 minbigg\ \| e_(j-1)p_3 + k ^top V_1\|, \| e_(j'-1)p_3 + k'^top V_1\|,\\ & \| e_(k-1)p_1 + i^top V_2 \|, \| e_(k'-1)p_1 + i^top V_2 \|, \| e_(i-1)p_2 + j^top V_3 \|, \| e_(i'-1)p_2 + j'^top V_3 \| bigg\. To see this, note that no matter how many overlapping indices there, there is always one set of indices that are not overlapping, and hence the variance can be lower bounded by at least one of sigma_min^2 times bigg\ &\| e_(j-1)p_3 + k ^top V_1\|^2, \| e_(j'-1)p_3 + k'^top V_1\|^2,\\ & \| e_(k-1)p_1 + i^top V_2 \|^2, \| e_(k'-1)p_1 + i^top V_2 \|^2, \| e_(i-1)p_2 + j^top V_3 \|^2, \| e_(i'-1)p_2 + j'^top V_3 \|^2 bigg\. Therefore, as long as minbigg\ &\| e_(j-1)p_3 + k ^top V_1\|^2, \|e_(j'-1)p_3 + k'^top V_1\|^2, \| e_(k-1)p_1 + i^top V_2 \|^2, \\ & \| e_(k'-1)p_1 + i^top V_2 \|^2, \| e_(i-1)p_2 + j^top V_3 \|^2, \| e_(i'-1)p_2 + j'^top V_3 \|^2 bigg\ \\ &gg maxbigg\ frackappa mu_0^2 r^3/2 log(p)p^3 , fracmu_0^5 r^3 kappa^2 log^3/2(p)(lambda/sigma)p^3/2, frackappa^4 mu_0^6 r^3 log(p)p^3, fracmu_0^8 kappa^6 r^3 log^2(p)(lambda/sigma)^2 p bigg\. we see all our results continue to hold. In particular, when kappa,mu_0 = O(1), it is sufficient to have that minbigg\ &\| e_(j-1)p_3 + k ^top V_1\|^2, \| e_(j'-1)p_3 + k'^top V_1\|^2, \| e_(k-1)p_1 + i^top V_2 \|^2, \\ & \| e_(k'-1)p_1 + i^top V_2 \|^2, \| e_(i-1)p_2 + j^top V_3 \|^2, \| e_(i'-1)p_2 + j'^top V_3 \|^2 bigg\ \\ &gg maxbigg\ fracr^3 log(p)p^3 , fracr^3 log^3/2(p)(lambda/sigma)p^3/2bigg\, which is precisely the condition in crefthm:entrytesting_v1.

nodes.statement: Without loss of generality we assume that sigma^2 equiv sigma^2_min, since otherwise we only increase the variance. In addition, we assume that the core tensor C in R^r_1 times r_2 times r_3 is known, since not knowing it will also only increase the variance. Next, by the Cramer-Rao lower bound, for any unbiased estimator (widetilde U_1, widetilde U_2, widetilde U_3) of the parameter (U_1, U_2, U_3), it holds that Var (widetilde U_1, widetilde U_2, widetilde U_3) &succcurlyeq I^-1, where I is defined via I &coloneqq E bigg[nabla_U_1, U_2,U_3 log L(widehat T; U_1, U_2, U_3)bigg] bigg[ nabla_U_1, U_2,U_3 log L(widehat T; U_1, U_2, U_3)bigg]^top, By the delta method, for any unbiased estimator check T_ijk of T_ijk it holds that Var(check T_ijk) geq nabla_U_1,U_2,U_3 T_ijk^top I^-1nabla_U_1,U_2,U_3 T_ijk, where nabla_U_1,U_2,U_3 T_ijk is the gradient of T_ijk with respect to the (vectorized) parameter (U_1, U_2,U_3). We now proceed in several steps. item Step 1: Calculating the Relevant Quantities: First, we note that fracpartial T_ijkpartial (U_1)_l_1,s &= fracpartialpartial (U_1)_l_1,s sum_a,b,c C_abc (U_1)_ia (U_2)_jb (U_3)_kc nonumber \\ &= I_i = l_1 sum_b,c C_sbc (U_2)_jb (U_3)_kc. A similar calculation can be made for the other modes, with appropriate replacements. We now calculate the Fisher information matrix. To do so, we will use the convention that the vectorized matrices U_1, U_2, and U_3 are in the order such that they are first indexed by row then by column, which will be a useful convention later on. We note that log f( widehat T; U_1, U_2, U_3, C ) &=frac-12sigma^2 sum_i_1,i_2,i_3 bigg( widehat T_i_1 i_2 i_3 - sum_a,b,c C_abc (U_1)_i_1 a (U_2)_i_2 b (U_3 )_i_3 c bigg)^2; and hence that &fracpartial partial (U_1)_l a'log f( widehat T; U_1, U_2, U_3, C ) \\ &= fracpartial partial (U_1)_l a'frac-12sigma^2 sum_i_1,i_2,i_3 bigg( widehat T_i_1 i_2 i_3 - sum_a,b,c C_abc (U_1)_i_1 a (U_2)_i_2 b (U_3 )_i_3 c bigg)^2 \\ &= frac-1sigma^2 sum_i_2,i_3 bigg( widehat T_l i_2 i_3 - sum_a,b,c C_abc (U_1)_l a (U_2)_i_2 b (U_3 )_i_3 c bigg)\\ & times fracpartialpartial(U_1)_la' bigg( widehat T_l i_2 i_3 - sum_a,b,c C_abc (U_1)_l a (U_2)_i_2 b (U_3 )_i_3 c bigg) \\ &= frac1sigma^2 sum_i_2,i_3 bigg( widehat T_l i_2 i_3 - sum_a,b,c C_abc (U_1)_l a (U_2)_i_2 b (U_3 )_i_3 c bigg) bigg( sum_b,c C_a' bc (U_2)_i_2 b (U_3 )_i_3 c bigg) \\ &= frac1sigma^2 sum_i_2, i_3 Z_l i_2 i_3 bigg( sum_b,c C_a' bc (U_2)_i_2 b (U_3 )_i_3 c bigg). Therefore, E &Bigg[ fracpartial partial (U_1)_l_1 a_1log f( widehat T; U_1, U_2, U_3, C ) fracpartial partial (U_1)_l_2 a_2log f( widehat T; U_1, U_2, U_3, C ) Bigg] nonumber \\ &= frac1sigma^4 E Bigg[ sum_i_2, i_3 Z_l_1 i_2 i_3 bigg( sum_b,c C_a_1 bc (U_2)_i_2 b (U_3 )_i_3 c bigg) Bigg] Bigg[ sum_i_2, i_3 Z_l_2 i_2 i_3 bigg( sum_b,c C_a_2 bc (U_2)_i_2 b (U_3 )_i_3 c Bigg] nonumber \\ &= frac1sigma^2 I_l_1 = l_2sum_i_2, i_3 bigg( sum_b,c C_a_1 bc (U_2)_i_2 b (U_3 )_i_3 c bigg) bigg( sum_b,c C_a_2 bc (U_2)_i_2 b (U_3 )_i_3 c bigg) nonumber \\ &= frac1sigma^2 I_l_1 = l_2sum_b,c C_a_1 bc C_a_2 bc where the second inequality uses the independence of Z_i_1i_2i_3, and the final inequality is by orthonormality. Similarly, &E Bigg[ fracpartial partial (U_1)_l_1 a_1log f( widehat T; U_1, U_2, U_3, C ) fracpartial partial (U_2)_l_2 b_1log f( widehat T; U_1, U_2, U_3, C ) Bigg] nonumber \\ &= frac1sigma^4 E Bigg[ sum_i_2, i_3 Z_l_1 i_2 i_3 bigg( sum_b,c C_a_1 bc (U_2)_i_2 b (U_3 )_i_3 c bigg) Bigg] Bigg[ sum_i_1, i_3 Z_i_1 l_2 i_3 bigg( sum_a,c C_a b_1 c (U_1)_i_1 a (U_3 )_i_3 c Bigg] nonumber\\ &= frac1sigma^2 sum_i_3 bigg(sum_b,c C_a_1 bc (U_2)_l_2 b (U_3)_i_3 c bigg) bigg( sum_a,c C_a b_1 c (U_1)_l_1 a (U_3 )_i_3 c bigg) Similar derivations can be obtained for U_2 and U_3. Define the r_1 vectors \c_a_i\_i=1^r_1 in R^r_2 r_3 by setting its (b,c) entry equal to C_a_i bc, and define the r_2 and r_3 vectors \c_b_j\_j=1^r_2 and \ c_c_k\_k=1^r_3 similarly. With this definition, we note that is simply the equation for the sample gram matrix for the r_1 vectors \c_a_i\_i=1^r_1 in R^r_2 r_3 (with similar observations for the other two modes). Therefore, abusing notation slightly, let I_1 in R^p_1 r_1 times p_1 r_1 be the block-diagonal matrix with r_1 times r_1 blocks given by this sample gram matrix, and let I_2 and I_3 be defined similarly. With these notations in place, we see that I can be written in the following form: sigma^2 I &= I_1 & 0 &0 \\ 0 & I_2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 &I_3 + 0 & H_12 & H_13 \\ H_12^top & 0 & H_23 \\ H_13^top & H_23^top & 0 , where H_12, H_13 and H_23 are of appropriate dimension with entries given by the identity in . item Step 2: Three Tensor Algebra Identities: We now simplify the expressions in , and . We recall from that fracpartial T_ijkpartial (U_1)_i,s &= sum_b,c C_sbc (U_2)_jb (U_3)_kc nonumber\\ &= sum_b,c bigg( sum_i_1i_2i_3 T_i_1 i_2 i_3 (U_1)_i_1 s (U_2)_i_2 b (U_3)_i_3 c bigg) (U_2)_jb (U_3)_kc nonumber\\ &= sum_b,c (U_2)_jb (U_3)_kc bigg( sum_i_1 (U_1)_i_1 s sum_i_2 i_3 T_i_1 i_2 i_3 (U_2)_i_2 b (U_3)_i_3 c bigg)nonumber \\ &= sum_b,c (U_2)_jb (U_3)_kc bigg( U_1^top T_1 (U_2 otimes U_3) bigg)_s, (b,c) nonumber\\ &= Bigg[ U_1^top T_1 (U_2 otimes U_3) (U_2 otimes U_3)^topBigg]_s,(j-1)p_3 + k nonumber\\ &= Bigg[ U_1^top U_1 Lambda_1 V_1 P_U_1 otimes U_2 Bigg]_s,(j-1)p_3 +k nonumber \\ &= bigg( Lambda_1 V_1^top bigg)_s,(j-1)p_3 +k. Here we have denoted the index (b,c) to be the matricization index corresponding to the s,b,c element of the underlying tensor. We now consider the form of the blocks in the definition of I_1. Recall that each block is given by the matrix whose (a_1, a_2) entry is equal to sum_b,c C_a_1 bc C_a_2bc. We have that &sum_b,c C_a_1 bc C_a_2bc \\ &= sum_b,c bigg( sum_i_1,i_2,i_3 T_i_1 i_2 i_3 (U_1)_i_1 a_1 (U_2)_i_2 b (U_3)_i_3 c bigg)bigg( sum_j_1,j_2,j_3 T_j_1 j_2 j_3 (U_1)_j_1 a_2 (U_2)_j_2 b (U_3)_j_3 c bigg) \\ &= sum_b,csum_i_1, i_2,i_3 T_i_1i_2i_3 (U_1)_i_1 a_1 (U_2 )_i_2 b (U_3 )_i_3bigg[ sum_j_1 (U_1)_j_1 a_2 sum_j_2 j_3 T_j_1 j_2 j_3 (U_2)_j_2b (U_3)_j_3 c bigg] \\ &= sum_b,csum_i_1, i_2,i_3 T_i_1i_2i_3 (U_1)_i_1 a_1 (U_2 )_i_2 b (U_3 )_i_3 bigg[ sum_j_1 (U_1)_j_1 a_2 bigg( T_1 (U_2 otimes U_3 ) bigg)_j_1,(b,c) bigg] \\ &= sum_b,csum_i_1, i_2,i_3 T_i_1i_2i_3 (U_1)_i_1 a_1 (U_2 )_i_2 b (U_3 )_i_3 bigg( U_1 ^top T_1 (U_2 otimes U_3)bigg)_a_2, (b,c) \\ &=sum_b,c bigg( U_1 ^top T_1 (U_2 otimes U_3)bigg)_a_2, (b,c) sum_i_1, i_2,i_3 T_i_1i_2i_3 (U_1)_i_1 a_1 (U_2 )_i_2 b (U_3 )_i_3 \\ &=sum_b,c bigg( U_1 ^top T_1 (U_2 otimes U_3)bigg)_a_2, (b,c) bigg( U_1^top T_1 (U_2 otimes U_3) bigg)_a_1, (b,c) \\ &= bigg(U_1^top T_1 ( U_2 otimes U_3 ) (U_2 otimes U_3)^top T_1^top U_1 bigg)_a_1a_2 \\ &= bigg( U_1^top U_1 Lambda_1 V_1 P_U_2 otimes U_3 V_1^top Lambda_1 U_1^top U_1 bigg)_a_1 a_2 \\ &= (Lambda_1^2)_a_1 a_2, where we have used the fact that T_1 P_U_2 otimes U_3 = T_1 and the fact that P_U_2 otimes U_3 = (U_2 otimes U_3) (U_2 otimes U_3)^top. This calculation reveals that I_1 is simply a diagonal matrix with repeated diagonal blocks of Lambda_1^2, with a similar observation holding for I_2 and I_3, with diagonal blocks equal to Lambda_2^2 and Lambda_3^2 respectively. Finally, we note that from that sigma^2 E Bigg[ fracpartial partial (U_1)_l_1 a_1&log f( widehat T; U_1, U_2, U_3, C ) fracpartial partial (U_1)_l_2 a_2log f( widehat T; U_1, U_2, U_3, C ) Bigg] \\ &= sum_i_3 bigg(sum_b,c C_a_1 bc (U_2)_l_2 b (U_3)_i_3 c bigg) bigg( sum_a,c C_a b_1 c (U_1)_l_1 a (U_3 )_i_3 c bigg). Note that sum_b,c C_a_1bc (U_2)_l_2 b (U_3)_i_3 c &= sum_b,c (U_2)_l_2 b (U_3)_i_3 c bigg( sum_j_1j_2j_3 T_j_1j_2j_3 (U_1)_j_1a_1 (U_2)_j_2 b (U_3)_j_3c bigg) \\ &= sum_b,c (U_2)_l_2 b (U_3)_i_3 c bigg( U_1^top T_1 (U_2 otimes U_3)bigg)_a_1,(b,c) \\ &= bigg( U_1^top T_1 (U_2 otimes U_3) (U_2 otimes U_3)^top bigg)_a_1,(l_2,i_3) \\ &= bigg( Lambda_1 V_1^top bigg)_a_1,(l_2,i_3) \\ &= (Lambda_1)_a_1 big( V_1big)_(l_2-1)p_3 + i_3, a_1. By a similar argument, bigg( sum_a,c C_a b_1 c (U_1)_l_1 a (U_3 )_i_3 c bigg) &= (Lambda_2)_b_1 big( V_2 big)_(l_1 - 1)p_2 + i_3. Therefore, sum_i_3 &bigg(sum_b,c C_a_1 bc (U_2)_l_2 b (U_3)_i_3 c bigg) bigg( sum_a,c C_a b_1 c (U_1)_l_1 a (U_3 )_i_3 c bigg) nonumber \\ &= sum_i_3(Lambda_2)_b_1 big( V_2 big)_(l_1 - 1)p_2 + i_3(Lambda_1)_a_1 big( V_1big)_(l_2-1)p_3 + i_3, a_1, with appropriate replacements for different modes. item Step 3: Inverting the Fisher Information Matrix: Recall that we have that sigma^2 I &= I_1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 &I_2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 &I_3 + 0 & H_12 & H_13 \\ H_12^top & 0 & H_23 \\ H_13^top & H_23^top & 0 \\ &coloneqq widetilde I + H. It is straightforward to observe that the matrix widetilde I is invertible since it is a diagonal matrix with positive elements.
